      package io.simpleide.lsp;
      
      import java.nio.file.Files;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.Map;
      
      import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assumptions.assumeTrue;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;
      
      import io.simpleide.lsp.client.LspClient;
      import io.simpleide.thread.ThreadMaster;
      
      /**
       * Starts every bundled language server and checks the LSP handshake and completion.
       *
       * <p>
       * Each test resolves the same install and launch command the IDE uses, starts the real
       * server as a subprocess, waits for the {@code initialize} response and opens a real
       * document before requesting completion. The tests are tagged {@code language-tools} and
       * {@code lsp}, and skip when the language runtime or the platform-specific server is not
       * available, matching the debug adapter integration tests.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      @Tag("language-tools")
      @Tag("lsp")
      class LspServerIntegrationTest {
      
        private static final String JAVA_SOURCE = """
            public class Main {
                public static void main(String[] args) {
                    String text = "a";
                    System.out.println(text.length());
                }
            }
            """;
      
        private static final String JAVASCRIPT_SOURCE = """
            const value = 1;
            console.log(value);
            """;
      
        private static final String PYTHON_SOURCE = """
            value = "text"
            value.upper()
            """;
      
        private static final String GO_SOURCE = """
            package main
      
            import "fmt"
      
            func main() {
              fmt.Println("hi")
            }
            """;
      
        private static final String KOTLIN_SOURCE = """
            fun main() {
                val text = "a"
                println(text.length)
            }
            """;
      
        private static final String GROOVY_SOURCE = """
            def text = "a"
            println(text.length())
            """;
      
        private static final String C_SOURCE = """
            #include <string.h>
      
            int main(void) {
                char *text = "a";
                strlen
                return 0;
            }
            """;
      
        private static final String CPP_SOURCE = """
            #include <string>
      
            int main() {
                std::string text = "a";
                text.
                return 0;
            }
            """;
      
        private static final String RUST_SOURCE = """
            fn main() {
                let text = "a";
                println!("{}", text.len());
            }
            """;
      
        private static final String CSHARP_SOURCE = """
            class Program {
                static void Main() {
                    string text = "a";
                    text.
                }
            }
            """;
      
        @BeforeAll
        @SuppressWarnings("unused")
        static void initializeThreadManager() {
          ThreadMaster.getInstance().initialize();
        }
      
        @TempDir
        Path workspace;
      
        @Test
        void initializesJavaAndAnswersCompletion() throws Exception {
          LspIntegrationHarness.requireToolchain("java", "-version");
          Path source = Files.writeString(workspace.resolve("Main.java"), JAVA_SOURCE);
      
          try (LspClient client = LspIntegrationHarness.start("java", workspace, Map.of())) {
            LspIntegrationHarness.assertAnswersCompletion(client, "java", source, JAVA_SOURCE, new Position(3, 15));
          }
        }
      
        @Test
        void initializesJavaScriptAndAnswersCompletion() throws Exception {
          LspIntegrationHarness.requireToolchain("node", "--version");
          Path source = Files.writeString(workspace.resolve("app.js"), JAVASCRIPT_SOURCE);
      
          try (LspClient client = LspIntegrationHarness.start("javascript", workspace, Map.of())) {
            LspIntegrationHarness.assertAnswersCompletion(client, "javascript", source, JAVASCRIPT_SOURCE,
                new Position(1, 8));
          }
        }

name: Debug CI

on:

permissions:

jobs:
  debug:
    name: Debug integration tests (latest toolchains)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: zulu
          java-version: "27"
          cache: maven

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: latest

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.x"

      # rust-analyzer cannot load the standard library without the rust-src
      # component, and then answers every completion request with null.
      - name: Set up Rust with rust-src
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rust-src
          rustup default stable

      # OmniSharp analyzes loose .cs files only when Mono's MSBuild instance is
      # available; without it the C# language-server test skips. The Ubuntu
      # archive does not ship msbuild, so Mono comes from the project's own
      # repository, whose stable-focal suite also serves newer Ubuntu releases.
      - name: Set up Mono with MSBuild for the C# language server
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates gnupg
          sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
          sudo gpg --homedir /tmp --no-default-keyring \
            --keyring /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg \
            --keyserver hkp://keyserver.ubuntu.com:80 \
            --recv-keys 3FA7E0328081BFF6A14DA29AA6A19B38D3D831EF
          echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg] https://download.mono-project.com/repo/ubuntu stable-focal main" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mono-official-stable.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y mono-complete
          mono --version | head -1
          msbuild --version | head -3

      - name: Run debug integration tests
        run: make test-debug

      - name: Run language-server integration tests
        run: make test-lsp

- path: simpleide/src/main/java/io/simpleide/lsp/client/JavaLspSnippets.java
  content: |
      package io.simpleide.lsp.client;
      
      import java.util.ArrayList;
      import java.util.List;
      import java.util.regex.Pattern;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItem;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItemKind;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.InsertTextFormat;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Range;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextEdit;
      
      /**
       * Java snippets offered next to the completions returned by the language server.
       *
       * <p>
       * The items are plain completion entries: they appear in the normal completion popup, are
       * filtered by the text being typed and only insert their text when accepted. They are not
       * expanded automatically. The {@code scanner} item declares a {@link java.util.Scanner}
       * field when it is offered in a type body and a local variable inside a method, adding
       * the {@code java.util.Scanner} import through an additional text edit when it is
       * missing.
       *
       * <p>
       * Covered by {@code JavaLspSnippetsTest}.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      final class JavaLspSnippets {
      
        private static final Pattern TYPE_DECLARATION = Pattern.compile("\\b(class|interface|enum|record)\\b");
      
        private static final String MAIN = "public static void main(String[] args) {}";
      
        private static final String SCANNER_IMPORT = "import java.util.Scanner;";
      
        private JavaLspSnippets() {
        }
      
        /**
         * Returns whether snippets are offered for a language.
         * @param languageId LSP language identifier
         * @return {@code true} for {@code java}
         */
        static boolean supports(String languageId) {
          return "java".equals(languageId);
        }
      
        /**
         * Builds the snippet items for a caret position.
         *
         * <p>
         * Items are omitted after member-access dots and when the document or caret is out of
         * range.
         * @param text document text
         * @param caret caret offset in the document
         * @return the snippet completion items, never {@code null}
         */
        static List<CompletionItem> completions(String text, int caret) {
          if (text == null || caret < 0 || caret > text.length() || isMemberAccess(text, caret)) {
            return List.of();
          }
      
          List<CompletionItem> items = new ArrayList<>();
          items.add(completion("sout", "System.out.println()", "Print to standard output"));
          items.add(completion("main", MAIN, "Application entry point"));
          items.add(completion("psvm", MAIN, "Application entry point"));
          items.add(completion("fori", "for (int i = 0; i < 0; i++) {}", "Indexed for loop"));
      
          boolean staticField = isTypeBody(text, caret);
          CompletionItem scanner = completion("scanner",
              "final " + (staticField ? "static " : "") + "Scanner SC = new Scanner(System.in);",
              "Read from standard input");
          TextEdit importEdit = scannerImport(text);
          if (importEdit != null) {
            scanner.setAdditionalTextEdits(List.of(importEdit));
          }
          items.add(scanner);
          return items;
        }
      
        private static CompletionItem completion(String label, String insertText, String detail) {
          CompletionItem item = new CompletionItem(label);
          item.setKind(CompletionItemKind.Snippet);
          item.setDetail(detail);
          item.setInsertText(insertText);
          item.setInsertTextFormat(InsertTextFormat.PlainText);
          item.setFilterText(label);
          return item;
        }
      
        /**
         * Checks whether the caret follows a member-access dot.
         */
        private static boolean isMemberAccess(String text, int caret) {
          int start = caret;
          while (start > 0 && Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(text.charAt(start - 1))) {
            start--;
          }
          return start > 0 && text.charAt(start - 1) == '.';
        }
      
        /**
         * Checks whether the caret is inside a type body rather than a method, constructor or
         * initializer body.
         */
        private static boolean isTypeBody(String text, int caret) {
          int depth = 0;
          int open = -1;
          for (int index = caret - 1; index >= 0; index--) {
            char character = text.charAt(index);
            if (character == '}') {
              depth++;
            }
            else if (character == '{') {
              if (depth == 0) {
                open = index;
                break;
              }
              depth--;
            }
          }
          if (open < 0) {
            return true;
          }
      
          int start = open - 1;
          while (start >= 0 && "{;}".indexOf(text.charAt(start)) < 0) {
            start--;
          }
          return TYPE_DECLARATION.matcher(text.substring(start + 1, open)).find();
        }
      
        /**
         * Builds the import edit that makes {@code Scanner} resolve.
         * @return the edit inserting the import after the package and import section, or
         * {@code null} when the import is already present
         */
        private static TextEdit scannerImport(String text) {
          String[] lines = text.split("\n", -1);
          int lastHeaderLine = -1;
          for (int index = 0; index < lines.length; index++) {
            String line = lines[index].strip();
            if (SCANNER_IMPORT.equals(line)) {
              return null;
            }
            if (line.startsWith("package ") || line.startsWith("import ")) {
              lastHeaderLine = index;
            }
          }
      
          int line = Math.min(lastHeaderLine + 1, lines.length - 1);
          return new TextEdit(new Range(new Position(line, 0), new Position(line, 0)), SCANNER_IMPORT + "\n");

      package io.simpleide.lsp.client;
      
      import java.util.ArrayList;
      import java.util.List;
      
      import javax.swing.text.BadLocationException;
      import javax.swing.text.JTextComponent;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItem;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.InsertReplaceEdit;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Range;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextEdit;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.jsonrpc.messages.Either;
      import org.fife.ui.autocomplete.BasicCompletion;
      import org.fife.ui.autocomplete.Completion;
      import org.fife.ui.autocomplete.DefaultCompletionProvider;
      import org.fife.ui.rsyntaxtextarea.RSyntaxTextArea;
      import org.slf4j.Logger;
      import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
      
      /**
       * Completion provider backed by items returned by an LSP server.
       *
       * <p>
       * Each {@link org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItem} is converted to an
       * {@link LspCompletionProvider.LspCompletion} with its insertion text, detail and
       * documentation. When the item carries a text edit range, the already entered text is
       * read from that range so the completion list filters against the text the server expects
       * to replace.
       *
       * <p>
       * Covered by {@code LspCompletionProviderTest}.
       *
       * @author LuisOtavio13
       * @since v1.0.0beta
       * @see <a href=
       * "https://github.com/BrunoRNS/SIMPLE-IDE/blob/main/docs/api/lsp.md">docs/api/lsp.md</a>
       */
      public class LspCompletionProvider extends DefaultCompletionProvider {
      
        private static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger(LspCompletionProvider.class);
      
        /**
         * Replaces the available completions with the items returned by the server.
         * @param items completion items to expose; labels that are null or blank are skipped
         */
        @SuppressWarnings("")
        public void setItems(List<CompletionItem> items) {
          clear();
          List<Completion> completions_ = new ArrayList<>();
          for (CompletionItem item : items) {
            if (item.getLabel() == null || item.getLabel().isBlank()) {
              continue;
            }
      
            String insertion = getInsertionText(item);
            String inputText = item.getFilterText() == null ? item.getLabel() : item.getFilterText();
            LspCompletion completion = new LspCompletion(this, insertion, item.getDetail(), getDocumentation(item),
                item, inputText);
            completions_.add(completion);
          }
          addCompletions(completions_);
        }
      
        private String getInsertionText(CompletionItem item) {
          String insertion = item.getInsertText();
          Either<TextEdit, InsertReplaceEdit> textEdit = item.getTextEdit();
          if (textEdit != null) {
            if (textEdit.isLeft() && textEdit.getLeft() != null) {
              insertion = textEdit.getLeft().getNewText();
            }
            else if (textEdit.isRight() && textEdit.getRight() != null) {
              insertion = textEdit.getRight().getNewText();
            }
          }
          if (insertion == null || insertion.isEmpty()) {
            insertion = item.getLabel();
          }
          if (item.getInsertTextFormat() == org.eclipse.lsp4j.InsertTextFormat.Snippet) {
            insertion = insertion.replaceAll("\\$\\{\\d+:([^}]*)\\}", "$1").replaceAll("\\$\\{\\d+\\}|\\$\\d", "");
          }
          return insertion;
        }
      
        private static Range getInsertRange(CompletionItem item) {
          Either<TextEdit, InsertReplaceEdit> textEdit = item.getTextEdit();
          if (textEdit == null) {
            return null;
          }
          if (textEdit.isLeft()) {
            return textEdit.getLeft() == null ? null : textEdit.getLeft().getRange();
          }
          return textEdit.getRight() == null ? null : textEdit.getRight().getInsert();
        }
      
        private static int getOffset(RSyntaxTextArea textArea, Position position) throws BadLocationException {
          int lineStart = textArea.getLineStartOffset(position.getLine());
          int offset = lineStart + position.getCharacter();
          if (offset > textArea.getLineEndOffset(position.getLine())) {
            throw new BadLocationException("LSP completion position exceeds line bounds.", offset);
          }
          return offset;
        }
      
        private String getDocumentation(CompletionItem item) {
          Either<String, org.eclipse.lsp4j.MarkupContent> documentation = item.getDocumentation();
          if (documentation == null) {
            return item.getDetail();
          }
          if (documentation.isLeft()) {
            return documentation.getLeft();
          }
          org.eclipse.lsp4j.MarkupContent markup = documentation.getRight();
          return markup == null ? item.getDetail() : markup.getValue();
        }
      
        /**
         * Completion exposed to the auto-completion UI with its original LSP item.
         *

      package io.simpleide.lsp.client;
      
      import java.util.List;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItem;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextEdit;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      
      /**
       * Tests {@link JavaLspSnippets}.
       */
      class JavaLspSnippetsTest {
      
        @Test
        void offersTheJavaSnippetsAsCompletionItems() {
          List<CompletionItem> items = JavaLspSnippets.completions("class Main {}\n", 0);
      
          assertThat(items).extracting(CompletionItem::getLabel)
            .containsExactly("sout", "main", "psvm", "fori", "scanner");
          assertThat(item(items, "sout").getInsertText()).isEqualTo("System.out.println()");
          assertThat(item(items, "main").getInsertText()).isEqualTo("public static void main(String[] args) {}");
          assertThat(item(items, "psvm").getInsertText()).isEqualTo("public static void main(String[] args) {}");
          assertThat(item(items, "fori").getInsertText()).isEqualTo("for (int i = 0; i < 0; i++) {}");
        }
      
        @Test
        void declaresTheScannerFieldAtTypeLevel() {
          String text = "class Main {\n    \n}\n";
          CompletionItem scanner = item(JavaLspSnippets.completions(text, text.indexOf("\n    ")), "scanner");
      
          assertThat(scanner.getInsertText()).isEqualTo("final static Scanner SC = new Scanner(System.in);");
        }
      
        @Test
        void declaresTheScannerVariableInsideAMethod() {
          String text = "class Main {\n    void run() {\n        \n    }\n}\n";
          CompletionItem scanner = item(JavaLspSnippets.completions(text, text.indexOf("\n        ")), "scanner");
      
          assertThat(scanner.getInsertText()).isEqualTo("final Scanner SC = new Scanner(System.in);");
        }
      
        @Test
        void importsScannerAfterTheExistingImportSection() {
          String text = "package demo;\n\nimport java.util.List;\n\nclass Main {}\n";
          CompletionItem scanner = item(JavaLspSnippets.completions(text, 0), "scanner");
      
          TextEdit edit = scanner.getAdditionalTextEdits().get(0);
          assertThat(edit.getNewText()).isEqualTo("import java.util.Scanner;\n");
          assertThat(edit.getRange().getStart()).isEqualTo(new Position(3, 0));
        }
      
        @Test
        void addsTheScannerImportAtTheTopWhenThereIsNoHeader() {
          CompletionItem scanner = item(JavaLspSnippets.completions("class Main {}\n", 0), "scanner");
      
          TextEdit edit = scanner.getAdditionalTextEdits().get(0);
          assertThat(edit.getRange().getStart()).isEqualTo(new Position(0, 0));
        }
      
        @Test
        void doesNotRepeatAnExistingScannerImport() {
          String text = "import java.util.Scanner;\n\nclass Main {}\n";
          CompletionItem scanner = item(JavaLspSnippets.completions(text, 0), "scanner");
      
          assertThat(scanner.getAdditionalTextEdits()).isNull();
        }
      
        @Test
        void offersNoSnippetsAfterAMemberAccessDot() {
          assertThat(JavaLspSnippets.completions("class Main {\n    void run() {\n        text.\n    }\n}\n",
              "class Main {\n    void run() {\n        text.".length()))
            .isEmpty();
        }
      
        @Test
        void onlySupportsJava() {
          assertThat(JavaLspSnippets.supports("java")).isTrue();
          assertThat(JavaLspSnippets.supports("kotlin")).isFalse();
        }
      
        private static CompletionItem item(List<CompletionItem> items, String label) {
          return items.stream().filter(item -> label.equals(item.getLabel())).findFirst().orElseThrow();
        }
      
      }

      package io.simpleide.lsp.client;
      
      import javax.swing.SwingUtilities;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItem;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.InsertTextFormat;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Range;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextEdit;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.jsonrpc.messages.Either;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      
      import io.simpleide.ui.editor.Editor;
      
      /**
       * Tests {@link io.simpleide.lsp.client.LspCompletionProvider}.
       */
      class LspCompletionProviderTest {
      
        @Test
        void mapsLspSnippetCompletionsIntoRsyntaxCompletions() {
          LspCompletionProvider provider = new LspCompletionProvider();
          CompletionItem item = new CompletionItem("println");
          item.setFilterText("print");
          item.setInsertText("println(${1:value})$0");
          item.setInsertTextFormat(InsertTextFormat.Snippet);
          item.setDetail("Prints a value");
          provider.setItems(java.util.List.of(item));
      
          var completion = provider.getCompletionByInputText("print").get(0);
      
          assertThat(completion.getReplacementText()).isEqualTo("println(value)");
          assertThat(completion.getInputText()).isEqualTo("print");
        }
      
        @Test
        void keepsServerCompletionsAlongsideTheJavaSnippets() throws Exception {
          SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(() -> {
            Editor editor = new Editor();
            editor.setText("ma");
            editor.setCaretPosition(2);
      
            LspCompletionProvider provider = new LspCompletionProvider();
            java.util.List<CompletionItem> items = new java.util.ArrayList<>(
                JavaLspSnippets.completions(editor.getText(), editor.getCaretPosition()));
            for (String label : java.util.List.of("Math", "map", "marker")) {
              items.add(new CompletionItem(label));
            }
            provider.setItems(items);
      
            assertThat(provider.getCompletions(editor)).extracting(completion -> completion.getInputText())
              .containsExactly("main", "map", "marker", "Math");
          });
        }
      
        @Test
        void keepsEveryCompletionWhenLabelsRepeatWithDifferentDescriptions() throws Exception {
          SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(() -> {
            Editor editor = new Editor();
            editor.setText("Ma");
            editor.setCaretPosition(2);
      
            LspCompletionProvider provider = new LspCompletionProvider();
            java.util.List<CompletionItem> items = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
            for (String detail : java.util.List.of("Application entry point", "A", "java.lang", "")) {
              CompletionItem duplicate = new CompletionItem("Main");
              duplicate.setDetail(detail);
              items.add(duplicate);
            }
            items.add(new CompletionItem("Math"));
            provider.setItems(items);
      
            assertThat(provider.getCompletions(editor)).extracting(completion -> completion.getInputText())
              .containsExactly("Main", "Main", "Main", "Main", "Math");
          });
        }
      
        @Test
        void usesLspTextEditRangeWhenReplacingCompletionPrefix() throws Exception {
          SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(() -> {
            Editor editor = new Editor();
            editor.setText("prefix suf");
            editor.setCaretPosition(editor.getDocument().getLength());
      
            LspCompletionProvider provider = new LspCompletionProvider();
            CompletionItem item = new CompletionItem("suggestion");
            item.setTextEdit(Either.forLeft(new TextEdit(
                new Range(new Position(0, 0), new Position(0, editor.getCaretPosition())), "suggestion")));
            provider.setItems(java.util.List.of(item));
      
            var completion = provider.getCompletionByInputText("suggestion").get(0);
      
            assertThat(completion.getAlreadyEntered(editor)).isEqualTo("prefix suf");
          });
        }
      
      }

      installation, `DapManager.DapUnavailableException` carries a user-facing message
      that `MainFrame` shows to the user.
      
      ## Java through the JDT language server
      
      Java debugging runs inside Eclipse JDT LS instead of a downloaded adapter:
      
      1. `vscode.java.startDebugSession` starts the debug server and returns its port.
      2. `vscode.java.resolveMainClass` resolves the main class of the open file.
      3. `vscode.java.resolveClasspath` returns the module and class paths.
      4. `DapSession` connects over TCP and sends `launch` with `mainClass`,
         `projectName`, `modulePaths`, `classPaths`, `cwd` and `console`.
      
      The language server already connected to the editor tab is reused; when the tab
      has none yet, `EditorManager.connectLanguageServer` connects one. Java debugging
      therefore requires an Eclipse JDT language server with the `vscode-java-debug`
      plugin loaded. Without it the commands are not registered and the IDE reports
      that the language server rejected the command. Neither JDT LS nor the plugin is
      downloaded by the IDE.
      
      ## Breakpoints
      
      Breakpoints are stored per editor in `Editor` and painted in the gutter icon
      column through `Gutter.addLineTrackingIcon`. They are visible for every supported
      language file.
      
      - Clicking the gutter toggles the breakpoint on the clicked line. The breakpoint
        column is the gutter's icon row header, which is a child component, so the
        mouse listeners are installed on the gutter and on its children.
      - The hovered line shows a translucent dot preview; selected lines show a solid
        red dot.
      - Toggling a breakpoint (F9 or gutter click) notifies the active `DapSession`
        through `setBreakpoints`, so the adapter always receives the current line set
        for the debugged file.
      
      ## Output and controls
      
      Adapter and debuggee output events are published to the shared `Output` queue, so
      the I/O tab renders them with the same `[OUTPUT]`, `[ERROR]` and `[DEBUG]`
      colours as normal program output. Session milestones appear as `[OUTPUT]`
      markers:
      
      | Marker | Meaning |
      | --- | --- |
      | `[OUTPUT] {INITIALIZED}` | The adapter completed the DAP handshake |
      | `[OUTPUT] {WAITING FOR STDIN}` | The debuggee is running and waiting for input; repeated after each forwarded line |
      | `[OUTPUT] {FINISHED}` | The session terminated or the user stopped it |
      
      `DapSession` sends `setBreakpoints` for the selected file and exposes `resume`,
      `pause`, `stepOver`, `stepInto`, `stepOut` and `close`, which back the debug
      buttons shown by `IOPanel` while a debug session is active. Step requests are
      ignored while the program is running; the I/O tab prints that execution is
      running.
      
      ## Tests
      
      - `DapRegistryTest` covers registry parsing, platform/architecture matching,
        command placeholders and bundled downloads.
      - `DapRegistryIntegrationTest` covers that every supported platform resolves to
        an adapter and that every adapter ships downloads for all OS/architecture
        combinations.
      - `DapLanguageRegistryTest` covers the four debuggable languages, transports,
        language mapping and that language-server adapters are never installed.
      - `DapManagerTest` covers unsupported-platform fallback without network access.
      - `DapInstallerTest` covers installed-version markers and cleanup after a
        rejected insecure download.
      - `DapSessionIntegrationTest` starts a real adapter process over `stdio` and
        `tcp` and exercises the whole session, including the execution controls and the
        output markers.
      - `DapIOPanelIntegrationTest` clicks every debug button against a live adapter.
      - `JavaDebugBridgeIntegrationTest` runs the Java path against a real TCP adapter
        and a stubbed language-server client.
      - `JsDebugAdapterIntegrationTest` debugs a real Node.js program with the installed
        `js-debug` adapter (tagged `language-tools`, skipped without `node`, without the
        adapter, or on an operating system and architecture with no registered adapter).
      - `IOPanelTest` and `InputForwarderTest` cover output colouring, input forwarding
        and debug-mode controls.

  content: |
      no standalone process to launch; use `startJava` for those.
      
      ## Java through the JDT language server
      
      The Java debug adapter is hosted by Eclipse JDT LS, so the IDE never downloads or
      launches it. `JavaDebugBridge` uses the workspace commands the language server
      exposes and then opens a `DapSession` over TCP on the returned port:
      
      1. `vscode.java.startDebugSession` starts the debug server and returns its port.
      2. `vscode.java.resolveMainClass` resolves the main class of the open file; the
         entry whose simple name matches the file name is preferred, otherwise the
         first one is used.
      3. `vscode.java.resolveClasspath` returns `[modulePaths, classPaths]`, which are
         forwarded to the adapter.
      4. The DAP `launch` request carries `mainClass`, `projectName`, `modulePaths`,
         `classPaths`, `cwd`, `name` and `console: internalConsole`.
      
      ```java
      JavaDebugClient client = (command, arguments) -> lspClient.executeCommand(command, arguments);
      DapSession session = manager.startJava(Path.of("src/App.java"), client, List.of(10), listener);
      ```
      
      `MainFrame` reuses the language server already connected to the tab, connecting
      one when the tab has none yet. When the language server fails a command, the
      session is not started and the error message names the failing step.
      
      ### Requirements
      
      Java debugging requires an Eclipse JDT language server that has the
      `vscode-java-debug` plugin loaded; otherwise `vscode.java.startDebugSession` is
      not registered and the IDE reports that the language server rejected the
      command. Providing JDT LS and the plugin is a user environment requirement and is
      not downloaded by the IDE, so the Java path is verified in the build only against
      a scripted adapter and a stubbed language-server client (see `Tests`).
      
      ## Breakpoints
      
      Breakpoints are stored per editor in `Editor` and painted in the gutter icon
      column through `Gutter.addLineTrackingIcon`:
      
      - Clicking any part of the gutter toggles the breakpoint of the clicked line.
        The breakpoint column is drawn by the gutter's icon row header, a child
        component, so `EditorTab` installs the mouse listeners on the gutter and on all
        of its children.
      - The line under the pointer shows a translucent dot as a preview; a selected
        line shows a solid red dot.
      - F9 toggles a breakpoint on the caret line.
      - Every toggle notifies the listener registered with
        `Editor.setBreakpointListener(Consumer<List<Integer>>)`, which `MainFrame`
        wires to `DapSession.setBreakpoints`, so the adapter receives the current line
        set for the debugged file.
      
      ## Output and controls
      
      Adapter and debuggee output is published to the shared `Output` queue, so the I/O
      tab renders it with the same `[OUTPUT]`, `[ERROR]` and `[DEBUG]` prefixes as
      normal program output. Session milestones are published as `[OUTPUT]` markers so
      the user can follow the handshake:
      
      | Marker | Published when |
      | --- | --- |
      | `[OUTPUT] {INITIALIZED}` | The adapter answered the DAP handshake with its `initialized` event |
      | `[OUTPUT] {WAITING FOR STDIN}` | The debuggee is running and its input is open, once after launch and again after each forwarded line |
      | `[OUTPUT] {FINISHED}` | The adapter reported `terminated`, or the session was closed by the user |
      
      `DapSession` exposes `resume`, `pause`, `stepOver`, `stepInto`, `stepOut` and
      `close`, which back the debug buttons shown by `IOPanel` while a debug session is
      active. Stepping requests are only sent while the adapter reported a stopped
      state; otherwise the I/O tab prints that execution is running.
      
      ## Tests
      
      - `DapRegistryTest` covers registry parsing, platform/architecture matching,
        command placeholders and bundled downloads.
      - `DapRegistryIntegrationTest` covers that every supported platform resolves to
        an adapter and that every adapter ships downloads for all OS/architecture
        combinations.
      - `DapLanguageRegistryTest` covers the four debuggable languages, their
        transports, source-file language mapping and that language-server adapters are
        never installed as processes.
      - `DapManagerTest` covers unsupported-platform fallback without network access.
      - `DapInstallerTest` covers installed-version markers and cleanup after a rejected
        insecure download.
      - `DapSessionIntegrationTest` starts a real adapter process over `stdio` and
        `tcp` and drives the full session: `initialize`, `launch`,
        `setBreakpoints`/`configurationDone`, `continue`, `next`, `stepIn`, `stepOut`,
        `pause`, breakpoint updates during a session, typed standard input reaching the
        live debuggee, and the `{INITIALIZED}`/`{WAITING FOR STDIN}`/`{FINISHED}`
        markers.
      - `DapIOPanelIntegrationTest` clicks every debug button in the I/O tab against a
        live adapter and checks the adapter received the matching request.
      - `JavaDebugBridgeIntegrationTest` runs the Java path end to end against a real
        TCP adapter and a stubbed language-server client, asserting the command
        sequence, the `mainClass`/`projectName` launch properties, breakpoints and
        execution controls.
      - `JsDebugAdapterIntegrationTest` debugs a real Node.js program with the installed
        `js-debug` adapter: it stops at a breakpoint, steps over, resumes and checks the
        program output. The test is tagged `language-tools` and skipped when the current
        operating system and architecture have no registered adapter, when the adapter
        is not installed, or when `node` is missing, so `make test-nolang` and headless

- path: docs/api/lsp.md
  content: |
      `simpleide/src/main/resources/io/simpleide/lsp/dowload/registry.json`. Each entry
      declares OS, architecture, minimum language version, version command, install
      strategy or URL, launch command and arguments.
      
      ### Extra Java snippets
      
      When a Java language server is connected, `LspEditorSupport` merges a few
      completion items of its own into every completion response: `psvm` and `main`
      insert `public static void main(String[] args) {}`, `sout` inserts
      `System.out.println()`, `fori` inserts `for (int i = 0; i < 0; i++) {}` and
      `scanner` inserts `final static Scanner SC = new Scanner(System.in);` at type
      level (or `final Scanner SC = ...` inside a method), adding the
      `java.util.Scanner` import through an additional text edit when it is missing.
      The items appear in the normal popup next to the server completions and only
      insert their text when accepted; they are offered for Java only, never after a
      member-access dot, and they are not expanded automatically.
      
      `LspCompletionProvider` orders completions by their input text so entries with
      repeating labels and different descriptions stay in the list instead of
      breaking the sorted search the completion window relies on.
      
      ## Connect a server
      
      ### Facade
      
      `io.simpleide.api.LanguageServers` wraps the shared manager, the registry and the
      file-to-language mapping in a few methods. Servers are installed on first use and
      one server process is shared per language and workspace.

      containing language keywords and common built-ins. The same keyword provider is
      used for every language when the JVM is headless. The fallback is not an LSP
      server and does not provide diagnostics, go-to-definition, formatting, or
      semantic completion.
      
      ## Server coverage
      
      The matrix below is the effective intersection of the registry and
      `LangPlatform`'s host detection. `x86` means 32-bit Intel, `x64` means 64-bit
      Intel, and `ARM64` covers `aarch64`/`arm64` registry names. A listed platform
      means a server definition exists; it does not guarantee that its runtime is
      installed or that the download/installation succeeds.
      
      | Language | Server | Linux | macOS | Windows | Runtime/version requirement |
      | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
      | Java | Eclipse JDT LS | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | JDT LS selects the highest compatible entry requiring Java 17 or 21. Windows x86 uses the local Java language-support fallback. |
      | Kotlin | kotlin-language-server | x86, x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x86, x64, ARM64 | Java 11 or newer. Initialization may take longer than a minute while the server indexes the workspace; the client allows up to 180 seconds. |
      | Groovy | groovy-language-server | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | — | Java 17 or newer; the registry builds the server from source after download with `gradlew -p <project directory>` and launches the resulting `*-all.jar`. |
      | JavaScript | typescript-language-server | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | Node.js 22.22.2 or newer. Windows x86 uses the local JavaScript language-support fallback. |
      | Python | Pyright | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | Node.js 14 or newer. Windows x86 uses keyword-based completion fallback. |
      | C# | OmniSharp (Mono) | x86, x64, ARM64 | x86, x64, ARM64 | x86, x64, ARM64 | Mono 6 or newer with an MSBuild instance; works without a .NET SDK and analyzes loose `.cs` files in the workspace folder. |
      | C | clangd | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x64 | The configured clangd release is installed from its platform archive. |
      | C++ | clangd | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x64 | Shares the clangd installation with C. |
      | Go | gopls | x86, x64, ARM64 | x86, x64, ARM64 | x86, x64, ARM64 | Go 1.26 or newer. Go 1.21 to 1.25 uses the pinned gopls 0.16.2 entry, which supports those toolchains. |
      | Rust | rust-analyzer | x64, ARM64 | x64, ARM64 | x86, x64, ARM64 | Uses platform-specific release assets; Windows x86 uses the i686 MSVC archive. Needs the `rust-src` component (`rustup component add rust-src`) for standard-library completion. |
      
      ### Coverage notes
      
      - The registry has no C/C++ server for Windows x86 or Windows ARM64, and no
        Groovy server for Windows.
      - The C# server is the Mono build of OmniSharp. It never downloads or requires a
        .NET SDK; OmniSharp still needs an MSBuild instance (the `msbuild` command from
        Mono, or a .NET SDK when one is installed) to load loose files. The Debug CI
        workflow installs Mono from the Mono project repository, where
        `mono-complete` also provides `msbuild`.
      - OmniSharp only analyzes files that belong to a project. When a C# folder has
        no `.sln`, `.csproj` or `.csx`, Simple IDE writes
        `SimpleIdeLooseFiles.csproj` next to the loose `.cs` files and includes them
        in it, so a single-file C# script gets completion. The file is not written
        when the folder already has a C# project.
      - Java, JavaScript, and Python have no language-server entry for Windows x86.
        Java and JavaScript use their bundled local language support there, and Python
        uses keyword-based completion.
      - Languages without bundled local language support receive keyword-based
        completion while an LSP is starting, when no server matches the host, or when
        a connection fails.
      - Some registry entries declare multiple equivalent architecture names.
      - rust-analyzer only discovers Cargo projects. When the workspace has no
        `Cargo.toml` or `rust-project.json`, each loose `.rs` file in the workspace
        folder is passed through the `linkedProjects` initialization option and

- path: docs/api/lsp.md
  content: |
      ## Completion
      
      `LspEditorSupport` requests completion after edits, maps LSP `CompletionItem`
      values to an RSTA completion provider, and applies the selected item. If you use
      your own editor:
      
      1. Send `didChange` with the new text and an incremented document version.
      2. Map the caret offset to an LSP `Position`.
      3. Send a `CompletionParams` request.
      4. Apply the chosen item's `textEdit` or `insertText` yourself.
      
      The bundled `LspCompletionProvider` and `LspTextEdit` show the mapping used by
      the application.
      
      ## Diagnostics
      
      `publishDiagnostics` gives a list of `Diagnostic` values with ranges, severity,
      message and optional code/source. `LspDiagnosticParser` converts them to RSTA
      squiggle underlines. A custom editor can keep the list and render it in its own
      way. Publish an empty list when a file becomes clean; do not leave stale
      diagnostics.
      
      ## Definition and formatting

      manager
          .connect(document, diagnostics -> {})
          .thenCompose(

+  private static List<String> compiledClassNames(Path classes) throws IOException {
+    List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
+    try (Stream<Path> files = Files.walk(classes)) {

+      }
+    }

Pronto. Rodei os testes primeiro e eles expuseram dois problemas reais; corrigi os dois e deixei tudo coberto.

## O que estava quebrado

1. **Debug Java em arquivo avulso não funcionava.** O JDT LS devolve `[]` para `vscode.java.resolveMainClass` em arquivos fora de projeto (confirmado no probe: `PROBE resolveMainClass=[]`), mas o código lançava o nome do arquivo como classe — que nunca foi compilada. O adapter então tentava rodar uma classe inexistente.
2. **Os snippets escondiam o LSP.** `withSnippets` mesclava os snippets mesmo quando o servidor devolvia lista vazia, então uma falha do JDT aparecia como um popup só com `psvm`/`sout` em vez de vazio.
3. **O teste real de debug Java nunca rodava:** ele não chamava `ThreadMaster.getInstance().initialize()`, então o nó de startup do LSP era registrado mas nunca agendado e o teste era *skipado* após 90 s de timeout.

## Correções

- `JavaDebugBridge`: quando o JDT não resolve classe principal, o arquivo é compilado com o compilador do JDK (`javax.tools`) em um diretório temporário `simpleide-java-debug-*`; a classe escolhida é a de mesmo nome do arquivo (ou a primeira classe top-level) e esse diretório vira o único `classPaths`. Sem compilador ou com erro de compilação, falha com mensagem clara antes do DAP.
- `LspEditorSupport.withSnippets`: snippets só entram quando a resposta do servidor tem itens; resposta vazia/nula passa intacta.
- `JavaRealDebugIntegrationTest`: inicializa o `ThreadMaster`; agora depura de verdade um `Main.java` avulso (breakpoint → resume → saída `doubled=2` → terminated).

## Testes adicionados

- `JavaDebugBridgeIntegrationTest`: compila arquivo avulso, usa `Main.class` do diretório compilado, e falha em arquivo que não compila.
- `LspEditorSupportSnippetsTest` (novo): snippets só com resposta real, nada em resposta vazia/nula, nada em outra linguagem ou após `.`.
- `LspCompletionProviderTest`: itens do servidor continuam visíveis junto dos snippets.
- `JavaLspSnippetsPopupIntegrationTest` (novo, JDT real): JDT responde completions em arquivo avulso, os snippets entram e o popup ainda mostra itens do servidor além de `psvm`.
- `LspServerIntegrationTest.reportsSyntaxErrorsInALooseJavaFile`: erro de sintaxe em `.java` avulso gera diagnóstico do JDT.

## Verificação executada

| Comando | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `make test-debug` | 21 testes, 0 falhas, 2 skips (Go não instalado aqui); inclui o debug real via JDT |
| `make test-lsp` | 12 testes, 0 falhas, 0 skips (Java completion, popup com snippets, diagnóstico) |
| `make test` | 448 testes, 0 falhas, 11 skips |
| `check-format` + import order | válidos; `debug.yml` validado como YAML |

## CI e docs

`.github/workflows/debug.yml` agora roda também os testes de snippet/popup antes de `make test-debug` (que já liga `-Dsimpleide.java.debug.real=true`) e `make test-lsp`. Documentei o comportamento de arquivo avulso e o guard dos snippets em `docs/api/dap.md`, `docs/reference/DAP.md`, `docs/api/lsp.md`, `docs/reference/LSP.md` e no `TODO_DEBUG_LSP.md`.

Limitações: não executei o GitHub Actions em si (só reproduzi os mesmos comandos localmente), e não validei em Windows/macOS. Cada debug de arquivo avulso compila para um diretório temporário novo, que não é apagado ao fim da sessão.

      /**
       * One running Debug Adapter Protocol session.
       *
       * <p>
       * The session launches the adapter process described by {@link DapAdapter}, connects to
       * it over standard input/output or TCP, and always starts the program with a
       * {@code launch} request; the {@code attach} request is never used. Output events are
       * forwarded to the shared {@link Output} API so the I/O tab can colour program output,
       * errors and IDE diagnostics.
       *
       * <p>
       * Execution control requests are safe to call from the Swing event dispatch thread; the
       * protocol requests are sent asynchronously by the LSP4J launcher.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      public final class DapSession implements AutoCloseable {
      
        private static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger(DapSession.class);
      
        private static final long START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30;
      
        /**
         * Adapters such as delve send the {@code initialized} event only after building the
         * program, so the wait must cover a cold Go build.
         */
        private static final long INITIALIZED_EVENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 90;
      
        /**
         * Loopback addresses tried when connecting to a server-style adapter. Adapters bind
         * either IPv4 (debugpy and delve) or IPv6 (the JavaScript adapter) loopback, so both
         * are attempted.
         */
        private static final List<String> LOOPBACK_HOSTS = List.of("127.0.0.1", "::1");
      
        /**
         * Sentinel for a thread that the adapter did not report yet. Thread {@code 0} is a
         * valid identifier for some adapters, so it cannot double as "unknown".
         */
        private static final int UNKNOWN_THREAD = -1;
      
        /**
         * Receives execution state changes from the adapter.
         *
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public interface Listener {
      
          /**
           * Called when the adapter reports that execution stopped.
           * @param threadId thread that stopped, or {@code 0} when the adapter did not
           * report a thread
           * @param reason stop reason reported by the adapter
           * @author BrunoRNS
           * @since v1.1.0
           */
          default void onStopped(int threadId, String reason) {
          }
      
          /**
           * Called when execution resumes.
           * @author BrunoRNS
           * @since v1.1.0
           */
          default void onContinued() {
          }
      
          /**
           * Called when the debug session ends.
           * @author BrunoRNS
           * @since v1.1.0
           */
          default void onTerminated() {
          }
      
        }
      
        private final DapAdapter adapter;
      
        private final Path installDirectory;
      
        private final Path program;
      
        private final Listener listener;
      
        private final int externalPort;
      
        private final Map<String, Object> externalLaunchArguments;
      
        private final Client client = new Client();
      
        private final Object stateLock = new Object();
      
        private final DapSession parent;
      
        private final List<DapSession> children = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
      
        private final AtomicReference<DapSession> controlTarget = new AtomicReference<>();
      
        private volatile int adapterPort;
      
        private volatile List<Integer> currentBreakpoints = List.of();
      
        private Process process;
      
        private Process debuggee;
      
        private Socket socket;
      
        private IDebugProtocolServer server;
      
        private Capabilities capabilities;
      
        private volatile int threadId = UNKNOWN_THREAD;
      
        private volatile boolean stopped;
      
        private volatile boolean closed;
      
        private final AtomicBoolean terminationNotified = new AtomicBoolean();
      
        private final AtomicBoolean finishedPublished = new AtomicBoolean();
      
        private final AtomicBoolean waitingForStdinPublished = new AtomicBoolean();
      
        private volatile boolean protocolStarted;
      
        private CompletableFuture<Void> initialized = new CompletableFuture<>();
      
        /**
         * Creates a session that has not started yet.
         * @param adapter adapter definition
         * @param installDirectory directory where the adapter is installed
         * @param program program to debug
         * @param listener listener for execution state changes, may be {@code null}
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public DapSession(DapAdapter adapter, Path installDirectory, Path program, Listener listener) {
          this(adapter, installDirectory, program, listener, null);
        }
      
        private DapSession(DapAdapter adapter, Path installDirectory, Path program, Listener listener, DapSession parent) {
          this.adapter = adapter;
          this.installDirectory = installDirectory;
          this.program = program;
          this.listener = listener == null ? new Listener() {
          } : listener;
          this.externalPort = 0;
          this.externalLaunchArguments = Map.of();
          this.parent = parent;
        }
      
        /**
         * Creates a session that connects to a debug adapter already listening on a port.
         *
         * <p>
         * This is used for adapters hosted by another process, such as the Java debug plugin
         * hosted by the JDT language server. The program starts with the supplied launch
         * arguments instead of a local adapter process.
         * @param program program being debugged
         * @param port TCP port where the adapter is listening
         * @param launchArguments properties sent in the DAP launch request
         * @param listener listener for execution state changes, may be {@code null}
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public DapSession(Path program, int port, Map<String, Object> launchArguments, Listener listener) {
          this(program, port, launchArguments, listener, null);
        }
      
        private DapSession(Path program, int port, Map<String, Object> launchArguments, Listener listener,
            DapSession parent) {
          this.adapter = null;
          this.installDirectory = null;
          this.program = program;
          this.listener = listener == null ? new Listener() {
          } : listener;
          this.externalPort = port;
          this.externalLaunchArguments = launchArguments == null ? Map.of() : Map.copyOf(launchArguments);
          this.parent = parent;
        }
      
        /**
         * Starts the adapter, initializes the protocol and launches the program.
         * @param breakpoints initial line breakpoints of the program
         * @throws IOException when the adapter process cannot be started or reached
         * @throws InterruptedException when the calling thread is interrupted
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public void start(List<Integer> breakpoints) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
          currentBreakpoints = breakpoints == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(breakpoints);
          if (externalPort > 0) {
            adapterPort = externalPort;
            connect(externalPort);
          }
          else {
            List<String> commandLine;
            int port = 0;
            if ("tcp".equals(adapter.getTransport())) {
              port = findFreePort();
              adapterPort = port;
              commandLine = adapter.commandLine(installDirectory.toString(), program.toString(), port);
              startProcess(commandLine, port);
              connect(port);
            }
            else {
              commandLine = adapter.commandLine(installDirectory.toString(), program.toString());
              startProcess(commandLine, port);
              synchronized (stateLock) {
                socket = null;
              }
            }
          }
      
          InputStream input;
          OutputStream output;
          synchronized (stateLock) {
            input = socket == null ? process.getInputStream() : socket.getInputStream();
            output = socket == null ? process.getOutputStream() : socket.getOutputStream();
          }
          Launcher<IDebugProtocolServer> launcher = DSPLauncher.createClientLauncher(client, input, output);
          synchronized (stateLock) {
            server = launcher.getRemoteProxy();
          }
          launcher.startListening();
      
          initialize();
          protocolStarted = true;
          CompletableFuture<Void> launchRequest = launch();
          awaitInitializedEvent();
          await(sendBreakpoints(program, breakpoints));
          if (capabilities != null && Boolean.TRUE.equals(capabilities.getSupportsConfigurationDoneRequest())) {
            await(server.configurationDone(new ConfigurationDoneArguments()));
          }
          await(launchRequest);
        }
      
        private void startProcess(List<String> commandLine, int port) throws IOException {
          ProcessBuilder builder = new ProcessBuilder(commandLine);
          builder.redirectErrorStream(false);
          Map<String, String> environment = adapter.environment(installDirectory.toString(), program.toString(), port);
          if (!environment.isEmpty()) {
            builder.environment().putAll(environment);
          }
          process = builder.start();
          drainErrors(process);
        }
      
        /**
         * Waits briefly for the adapter's {@code initialized} event.
         *
         * <p>
         * Most adapters send the event right after the {@code initialize} response, but some
         * send it only once the launch request arrives. Since the event only delays the
         * launch request, a bounded wait keeps those adapters working instead of blocking
         * startup.
         * @throws InterruptedException when the calling thread is interrupted
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        private void awaitInitializedEvent() throws InterruptedException {
          try {
            initialized.get(INITIALIZED_EVENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
          }
          catch (InterruptedException error) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw error;
          }
          catch (TimeoutException error) {
            LOGGER.debug("The debug adapter did not send the initialized event before launch.");
          }
          catch (ExecutionException error) {
            LOGGER.debug("The debug adapter failed to initialize.", error);
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Starts the nested debug session an adapter asks for with {@code startDebugging}.
         *
         * <p>
         * Adapters such as the JavaScript adapter launch the debuggee as a child session:
         * they send a {@code startDebugging} request with the child configuration and expect
         * the client to open a new session for it. The child session connects to the same
         * adapter port, inherits the current breakpoints and delegates execution controls
         * back to the parent while it is the session that stopped.
         * @param arguments child session request sent by the adapter
         * @throws IOException when the child session cannot be started
         * @throws InterruptedException when the calling thread is interrupted
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        private void startChildSession(StartDebuggingRequestArguments arguments) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
          if (arguments == null || arguments.getConfiguration() == null) {
            throw new IOException("The debug adapter requested a child session without a configuration.");
          }
          int port = adapterPort;
          if (port <= 0) {
            throw new IOException("Child debug sessions require a debug adapter reached over TCP.");
          }
          Map<String, Object> configuration = new LinkedHashMap<>(arguments.getConfiguration());
          DapSession child = new DapSession(program, port, configuration, listener, this);
          children.add(child);
          child.start(currentBreakpoints);
          LOGGER.debug("Started a child debug session for {}.", program);
        }
      
        private RunInTerminalResponse startDebuggee(RunInTerminalRequestArguments arguments) throws IOException {
          if (arguments == null || arguments.getArgs() == null || arguments.getArgs().length == 0) {
            throw new IOException("The debug adapter did not provide a program command.");
          }
          ProcessBuilder builder = new ProcessBuilder(Arrays.asList(arguments.getArgs()));
          if (arguments.getCwd() != null && !arguments.getCwd().isBlank()) {
            builder.directory(Path.of(arguments.getCwd()).toFile());
          }
          if (arguments.getEnv() != null) {
            builder.environment().putAll(arguments.getEnv());
          }
          Process launched = builder.start();
          synchronized (stateLock) {
            if (closed) {
              launched.destroyForcibly();
              throw new IOException("Debug session closed before its program started.");
            }
            if (debuggee != null && debuggee.isAlive()) {
              launched.destroyForcibly();
              throw new IOException("A debugged program is already running.");
            }
            debuggee = launched;
          }
          drainDebuggeeStream(launched.getInputStream(), OutputType.OUTPUT, "simpleide-debuggee-stdout");
          drainDebuggeeStream(launched.getErrorStream(), OutputType.ERROR, "simpleide-debuggee-stderr");
          startDebuggeeInputForwarder(launched);
      
          RunInTerminalResponse response = new RunInTerminalResponse();
          long processId = launched.pid();
          if (processId <= Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
            response.setProcessId((int) processId);
          }
          return response;
        }
      
        private void drainDebuggeeStream(InputStream stream, OutputType type, String threadName) {
          Thread drainThread = new Thread(() -> {
            try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(stream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
              String line;
              while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
                Output.getInstance().publish(type, line);
              }
            }
            catch (IOException error) {
              if (!closed) {
                LOGGER.debug("Unable to read debugged program output.", error);
              }
            }
          }, threadName);
          drainThread.setDaemon(true);
          drainThread.start();
        }
      
        private void startDebuggeeInputForwarder(Process launched) {
          Thread inputThread = new Thread(() -> {
            try (BufferedWriter writer = new BufferedWriter(
                new OutputStreamWriter(launched.getOutputStream(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
              publishWaitingForStdin();
              while (!closed && launched.isAlive()) {
                String line = Input.getInstance().get(1);
                if (line != null) {
                  writer.write(line);
                  writer.newLine();
                  writer.flush();
                  waitingForStdinPublished.set(false);
                  publishWaitingForStdin();
                }
              }
            }
            catch (InterruptedException error) {
              Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            }
            catch (IOException error) {
              if (!closed && launched.isAlive()) {
                LOGGER.debug("Unable to forward input to the debugged program.", error);
                Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.ERROR, "Unable to forward input to the debugged program.");
              }
            }
          }, "simpleide-debuggee-stdin");
          inputThread.setDaemon(true);
          inputThread.start();
        }
      
        private void drainErrors(Process started) {
          Runnable drain = () -> {
            try (InputStream errors = started.getErrorStream()) {
              byte[] buffer = new byte[4096];
              int read;
              while ((read = errors.read(buffer)) != -1) {
                String text = new String(buffer, 0, read, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).stripTrailing();
                if (!text.isBlank()) {
                  LOGGER.debug("[DAP] {}", text);
                  Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.DEBUG, text);
                }
              }
            }
            catch (IOException error) {
              if (!closed) {
                LOGGER.debug("[DAP] Unable to read adapter diagnostics.", error);
              }
            }
          };
          Thread drainThread = new Thread(drain, "simpleide-dap-stderr");
          drainThread.setDaemon(true);
          drainThread.start();
        }
      
        private void connect(int port) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
          IOException lastError = null;
          for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 100; attempt++) {
            if (closed) {
              throw new IOException("Debug session was closed before the adapter started.");
            }
            for (String host : LOOPBACK_HOSTS) {
              try {
                Socket candidate = new Socket();
                candidate.connect(new InetSocketAddress(host, port), 500);
                synchronized (stateLock) {
                  socket = candidate;
                }
                return;
              }
              catch (IOException error) {
                lastError = error;
              }
            }
            Thread.sleep(100);
          }
          throw new IOException("Unable to connect to the debug adapter on port " + port, lastError);

        private void initialize() throws IOException, InterruptedException {

          arguments.setLinesStartAt1(true);
          arguments.setColumnsStartAt1(true);

        private CompletableFuture<Void> launch() {
          Map<String, Object> arguments;

            arguments = new LinkedHashMap<>(externalLaunchArguments);

          else {
            arguments = new LinkedHashMap<>(adapter.launchArguments(program));
            arguments.putIfAbsent("program", program.toString());
            arguments.putIfAbsent("cwd", program.getParent() == null ? "." : program.getParent().toString());

        /**

         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public void setBreakpoints(Path file, List<Integer> lines) {
          currentBreakpoints = lines == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(lines);
          for (DapSession child : children) {
            child.setBreakpoints(file, lines);
          }
          sendBreakpoints(file, lines).whenComplete((response, error) -> {
            if (error != null) {
              LOGGER.warn("Unable to set debug breakpoints for {}.", file, error);
              return;
            }
            if (response != null && response.getBreakpoints() != null) {
              for (Breakpoint breakpoint : response.getBreakpoints()) {
                if (Boolean.FALSE.equals(breakpoint.isVerified())) {

                }

            }

        private CompletableFuture<SetBreakpointsResponse> sendBreakpoints(Path file, List<Integer> lines) {
          IDebugProtocolServer activeServer;
          synchronized (stateLock) {
            activeServer = server;
          }
          if (activeServer == null || file == null) {
            return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(null);
          }
          Source source = new Source();
          source.setName(file.getFileName().toString());
          source.setPath(file.toString());
          List<SourceBreakpoint> sourceBreakpoints = new ArrayList<>();
          for (Integer line : lines == null ? List.<Integer>of() : lines) {
            if (line != null && line > 0) {
              SourceBreakpoint breakpoint = new SourceBreakpoint();
              breakpoint.setLine(line);
              sourceBreakpoints.add(breakpoint);
            }
          }
          SetBreakpointsArguments arguments = new SetBreakpointsArguments();
          arguments.setSource(source);
          arguments.setBreakpoints(sourceBreakpoints.toArray(SourceBreakpoint[]::new));
          return activeServer.setBreakpoints(arguments);

        /**

        public boolean supportsConfigurationDone() {

        private void sendWhenStopped(java.util.function.IntFunction<CompletableFuture<Void>> request) {
          if (!stopped) {
            Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.DEBUG, "Execution is running; pause before stepping.");
            return;
          }
          sendUsingThread(request);
        }
      
        private void sendUsingThread(java.util.function.IntFunction<CompletableFuture<Void>> request) {
          IDebugProtocolServer activeServer;
          synchronized (stateLock) {
            activeServer = server;
          }
          if (activeServer == null || closed) {
            return;
          }
          int activeThread = threadId;
          if (activeThread >= 0) {
            sendRequest(request, activeThread);
            return;
          }
          activeServer.threads().whenComplete((response, error) -> {
            if (error != null) {
              publishControlFailure(error);
              return;
            }
            int resolved = firstThreadId(response);
            if (resolved < 0) {
              Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.DEBUG, "No debug thread is available for this request.");
              return;
            }
            threadId = resolved;
            sendRequest(request, resolved);
          });
        }
      
        private void sendRequest(java.util.function.IntFunction<CompletableFuture<Void>> request, int activeThread) {
          try {
            request.apply(activeThread).whenComplete((ignored, error) -> {
              if (error != null) {
                publishControlFailure(error);
              }
            });
          }
          catch (RuntimeException error) {
            publishControlFailure(error);

        private void publishControlFailure(Throwable error) {
          LOGGER.warn("Debug control request failed.", error);
          Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.ERROR, "Debug control request failed: " + error.getMessage());
        }
      
        private static int firstThreadId(org.eclipse.lsp4j.debug.ThreadsResponse response) {
          if (response == null || response.getThreads() == null || response.getThreads().length == 0) {
            return UNKNOWN_THREAD;
          }
          for (org.eclipse.lsp4j.debug.Thread thread : response.getThreads()) {
            if (thread != null && thread.getId() >= 0) {
              return thread.getId();
            }

          return UNKNOWN_THREAD;
        }
      
        private <T> T await(CompletableFuture<T> future) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
          try {
            return future.get(START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
          }
          catch (InterruptedException error) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw error;
          }
          catch (TimeoutException error) {
            throw new IOException("The debug adapter did not answer in time.", error);
          }
          catch (ExecutionException error) {
            Throwable cause = error.getCause() == null ? error : error.getCause();
            throw new IOException("The debug adapter rejected a protocol request: " + cause.getMessage(), cause);
          }
        }
      
        private static int findFreePort() throws IOException {
          try (ServerSocket socket = new ServerSocket(0)) {
            socket.setReuseAddress(true);
            return socket.getLocalPort();
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Ends the session, terminating the debugged program and the adapter process.
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0

        @Override
        public void close() {
          synchronized (stateLock) {
            if (closed) {
              return;
            }
            closed = true;
          }
          for (DapSession child : children) {
            child.close();
          }
          children.clear();
          IDebugProtocolServer activeServer = server;
          if (activeServer != null) {
            try {
              DisconnectArguments arguments = new DisconnectArguments();
              arguments.setTerminateDebuggee(true);
              activeServer.disconnect(arguments);
            }
            catch (RuntimeException error) {
              LOGGER.debug("Unable to disconnect from the debug adapter cleanly.", error);
            }
          }
          closeQuietly(socket);
          terminateProcess(debuggee);
          debuggee = null;
          terminateProcess(process);
          process = null;
          notifyTerminated();
          if (protocolStarted) {

          }
        }
      
        private void publishWaitingForStdin() {
          if (waitingForStdinPublished.compareAndSet(false, true)) {

        }
      
        private void publishFinished() {
          if (parent == null && finishedPublished.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
            Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.OUTPUT, Output.FINISHED);
          }
        }
      
        private static void terminateProcess(Process activeProcess) {
          if (activeProcess == null || !activeProcess.isAlive()) {
            return;
          }
          activeProcess.destroy();
          Thread terminator = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
              if (!activeProcess.waitFor(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) {
                activeProcess.destroyForcibly();
              }
            }
            catch (InterruptedException error) {
              Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
              activeProcess.destroyForcibly();
            }
          }, "simpleide-dap-process-stop");
          terminator.setDaemon(true);
          terminator.start();
        }
      
        private void notifyTerminated() {
          if (terminationNotified.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
            listener.onTerminated();
          }
        }
      
        private static void closeQuietly(Socket socket) {
          if (socket == null) {
            return;
          }
          try {
            socket.close();
          }
          catch (IOException error) {
            LOGGER.debug("Unable to close the debug adapter connection cleanly.", error);
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Client endpoint that translates adapter events into shared output and listener
         * calls.
         */
        private final class Client implements IDebugProtocolClient {
      
          @Override
          public void initialized() {
            if (parent == null) {
              Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.OUTPUT, Output.INITIALIZED);
            }
            initialized.complete(null);
          }
      
          @Override
          public void output(OutputEventArguments arguments) {
            if (arguments == null || arguments.getOutput() == null) {
              return;
            }
            OutputType type = "stderr".equalsIgnoreCase(arguments.getCategory()) ? OutputType.ERROR
                : "telemetry".equalsIgnoreCase(arguments.getCategory())
                    || "console".equalsIgnoreCase(arguments.getCategory()) ? OutputType.DEBUG
                        : OutputType.OUTPUT;
            for (String line : arguments.getOutput().split("\\R", -1)) {
              if (!line.isEmpty()) {
                Output.getInstance().publish(type, line);
              }
            }
          }
      
          @Override
          public void stopped(StoppedEventArguments arguments) {
            stopped = true;
            if (parent != null) {
              // Execution controls follow the session that actually stopped, which for
              // adapters that launch the debuggee as a child session is the child.
              parent.controlTarget.set(DapSession.this);
            }
            String reason = arguments == null || arguments.getReason() == null ? "unknown" : arguments.getReason();
            if (arguments != null && arguments.getThreadId() != null && arguments.getThreadId() >= 0) {
              threadId = arguments.getThreadId();
            }
            Output.getInstance().publish(OutputType.DEBUG, "Stopped: " + reason);
            listener.onStopped(threadId < 0 ? 0 : threadId, reason);
          }
      
          @Override
          public void continued(org.eclipse.lsp4j.debug.ContinuedEventArguments arguments) {
            stopped = false;
            if (parent != null) {
              parent.controlTarget.compareAndSet(DapSession.this, null);
            }
            listener.onContinued();
          }
      
          @Override
          public void terminated(TerminatedEventArguments arguments) {
            stopped = false;
            if (parent != null) {
              parent.controlTarget.compareAndSet(DapSession.this, null);
            }

            notifyTerminated();
            publishFinished();

           * @return the launched process information
           * @author BrunoRNS
           * @since v1.1.0

          @Override
          public CompletableFuture<Void> startDebugging(StartDebuggingRequestArguments arguments) {

              try {
                startChildSession(arguments);
                started.complete(null);

              catch (InterruptedException error) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();

              }
              catch (IOException | RuntimeException error) {
                started.completeExceptionally(error);

            }, "simpleide-dap-child-session");
            launcher.setDaemon(true);
            launcher.start();
            return started;
          }
      
          @Override
          public CompletableFuture<RunInTerminalResponse> runInTerminal(RunInTerminalRequestArguments arguments) {
            try {
              return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(startDebuggee(arguments));
            }
            catch (IOException | RuntimeException error) {
              return CompletableFuture.failedFuture(error);
            }
          }
      
        }

        public DapDownload downloadFor(LangPlatform platform) {
          if (platform == null || platform == LangPlatform.UNKNOWN) {
