      package io.simpleide.dap;
      
      import java.nio.file.Files;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.List;
      import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;
      import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assumptions.assumeTrue;
      
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.config.LangPlatform;
      import io.simpleide.language.io.Output;
      
      /**
       * Debugs a real Go program with the delve adapter installed by the IDE.
       *
       * <p>
       * The adapter is resolved from the bundled registry, installed on first use and started
       * as a real {@code dlv dap} process over TCP. The test is tagged {@code language-tools}
       * and is skipped when the platform has no registered delve download, when the local Go
       * toolchain is missing, or when the adapter cannot be installed.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      @Tag("language-tools")
      @Tag("debug")
      class GoDebugAdapterIntegrationTest {
      
        @TempDir
        Path tempDirectory;
      
        private final List<String> published = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
      
        private final List<String> events = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
      
        private AutoCloseable outputSubscription;
      
        @BeforeEach
        void subscribeToOutput() {
          published.clear();
          events.clear();
          outputSubscription = Output.getInstance().addListener(line -> published.add(line.text()));
        }
      
        @Test
        void stopsAtABreakpointAndFinishesARealGoProgram() throws Exception {
          DapAdapter adapter = registeredAdapter();
          assumeTrue(commandAvailable("go"), "go is not available on PATH");
          assumeTrue(goVersionAtLeast(25), "delve 1.27.2 requires Go 1.25 or newer; detected " + goVersion());
          Files.writeString(tempDirectory.resolve("go.mod"), "module debugdemo\n\ngo 1.21\n");
          Path program = Files.writeString(tempDirectory.resolve("main.go"), """
              package main
      
              import "fmt"
      
              func main() {
                value := 1
                doubled := value * 2
                fmt.Printf("doubled=%d\\n", doubled)
              }
              """);
          DapManager manager = new DapManager(DapRegistry.loadDefault(), LangPlatform.getCurrentPlatform());
          DapManager.PreparedAdapter prepared;
          try {
            prepared = manager.prepare(program);
          }
          catch (DapManager.DapUnavailableException error) {
            assumeTrue(false, "The delve adapter could not be installed: " + error.getMessage());
            return;
          }
          assertThat(prepared.adapter().getId()).isEqualTo(adapter.getId());
      
          DapSession session = new DapSession(prepared.adapter(), prepared.installDirectory(), program,
              new DapSession.Listener() {
                @Override
                public void onStopped(int threadId, String reason) {
                  events.add("stopped:" + reason);
                }
      
                @Override
                public void onTerminated() {
                  events.add("terminated");
                }
              });
          try (AutoCloseable subscription = outputSubscription) {
            session.start(List.of(7));
            await().atMost(90, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(events).contains("stopped:breakpoint"));
      
            session.resume();
            await().atMost(90, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(events).contains("terminated"));
            await().atMost(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
              .untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(published).anyMatch(line -> line.contains("doubled=2")));
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
        }
      
        @Test
        void stopsAtABreakpointInAStandaloneFileWithoutAModule() throws Exception {
          DapAdapter adapter = registeredAdapter();
          assumeTrue(commandAvailable("go"), "go is not available on PATH");
          assumeTrue(goVersionAtLeast(25), "delve 1.27.2 requires Go 1.25 or newer; detected " + goVersion());
          Path program = Files.writeString(tempDirectory.resolve("standalone.go"), """
              package main
      
              import "fmt"
      
              func main() {
                value := 1
                doubled := value * 2
                fmt.Printf("doubled=%d\\n", doubled)
              }
              """);
          DapManager manager = new DapManager(DapRegistry.loadDefault(), LangPlatform.getCurrentPlatform());
          DapManager.PreparedAdapter prepared;
          try {
            prepared = manager.prepare(program);
          }
          catch (DapManager.DapUnavailableException error) {
            assumeTrue(false, "The delve adapter could not be installed: " + error.getMessage());
            return;
          }
          assertThat(prepared.adapter().getId()).isEqualTo(adapter.getId());
          assertThat(prepared.adapter().launchArguments(program)).containsEntry("program", program.toString());
      
          DapSession session = new DapSession(prepared.adapter(), prepared.installDirectory(), program,
              new DapSession.Listener() {
                @Override
                public void onStopped(int threadId, String reason) {
                  events.add("stopped:" + reason);
                }
      
                @Override
                public void onTerminated() {
                  events.add("terminated");
                }
              });
          try (AutoCloseable subscription = outputSubscription) {
            session.start(List.of(7));
            await().atMost(90, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(events).contains("stopped:breakpoint"));
      
            session.resume();
            await().atMost(90, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(events).contains("terminated"));
            await().atMost(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
              .untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(published).anyMatch(line -> line.contains("doubled=2")));
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
        }
      
        private DapAdapter registeredAdapter() {
          DapAdapter adapter = DapRegistry.loadDefault().findForPlatform(LangPlatform.getCurrentPlatform(), "go");
          assumeTrue(adapter != null,
              "No Go debug adapter is registered for " + LangPlatform.getCurrentPlatform().getDisplayName());
          return adapter;
        }
      
        private static boolean commandAvailable(String command) {
          try {
            Process process = new ProcessBuilder(command, "version").redirectErrorStream(true).start();
            return process.waitFor(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS) && process.exitValue() == 0;
          }
          catch (Exception error) {
            return false;
          }
        }
      
        private static String goVersion() {
          try {
            Process process = new ProcessBuilder("go", "version").redirectErrorStream(true).start();
            java.io.InputStream input = process.getInputStream();
            byte[] buffer = new byte[256];
            int read = input.read(buffer);
            process.waitFor(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
            if (read <= 0) {
              return "unknown";
            }
            String output = new String(buffer, 0, read, java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            java.util.regex.Matcher matcher = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile("go version go(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)")
              .matcher(output);
            if (matcher.find()) {
              return matcher.group(1) + "." + matcher.group(2);
            }
            return output.trim();
          }
          catch (Exception error) {
            return "unknown";
          }
        }
      
        private static boolean goVersionAtLeast(int minor) {
          String version = goVersion();
          java.util.regex.Matcher matcher = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile("go version go(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)")
            .matcher(version);
          if (!matcher.find()) {
            return false;
          }
          return Integer.parseInt(matcher.group(2)) >= minor;
        }
      
      }
      
- path: simpleide/src/test/java/io/simpleide/dap/FakeDapServer.java
  content: |
      package io.simpleide.dap;
      
      import java.io.BufferedInputStream;
      import java.io.IOException;
      import java.io.InputStream;
      import java.io.OutputStream;
      import java.net.ServerSocket;
      import java.net.Socket;
      import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.ArrayList;
      import java.util.List;
      import java.util.Locale;
      
      import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
      import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
      import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ArrayNode;
      import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;
      
      /**
       * Scripted Debug Adapter Protocol server used by the DAP integration tests.
       *
       * <p>
       * The server speaks real DAP framing over standard input/output or TCP and behaves like a
       * small but complete debug adapter: it completes the {@code initialize} handshake,
       * answers {@code launch}, records {@code setBreakpoints}, reports a {@code stopped} event
       * after {@code configurationDone}, and answers every execution control request
       * ({@code continue}, {@code next}, {@code stepIn}, {@code stepOut}, {@code pause},
       * {@code threads} and {@code stackTrace}) with the events a real adapter emits.
       *
       * <p>
       * Every control request is echoed as a {@code stdout} output event ({@code {CONTROL}
       * next} and so on), so tests can observe from the IDE output queue that the adapter
       * really received the command. The same technique reports the breakpoint set the client
       * sent. When started with {@code --stdin-echo <classpath>} the adapter asks the client to
       * start {@link EchoStdin} through {@code runInTerminal}, which lets tests exercise real
       * standard input forwarding against a live debuggee process.
       *
       * <p>
       * It is launched as a child process, which keeps the tests independent of any external
       * debug adapter.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      public final class FakeDapServer {
      
        private static final ObjectMapper MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();
      
        private final InputStream input;
      
        private final OutputStream output;
      
        private final String echoClasspath;
      
        private final boolean terminateAfterStop;
      
        private final List<Integer> breakpoints = new ArrayList<>();
      
        private int sequence;
      
        private int currentLine = 1;
      
        private boolean terminatedSent;
      
        FakeDapServer(InputStream input, OutputStream output, String echoClasspath, boolean terminateAfterStop) {
          this.input = new BufferedInputStream(input);
          this.output = output;
          this.echoClasspath = echoClasspath;
          this.terminateAfterStop = terminateAfterStop;
        }
      
        /**
         * Runs the fake adapter.
         * @param args {@code tcp <port>} for a TCP server (or no arguments for stdio), plus
         * optional {@code --stdin-echo <classpath>}
         * @throws IOException when the transport cannot be opened
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
          int port = 0;
          String echoClasspath = null;
          boolean tcp = false;
          boolean terminateAfterStop = false;
          for (int index = 0; index < args.length; index++) {
            switch (args[index]) {
              case "tcp" -> {
                tcp = true;
                if (index + 1 < args.length) {
                  port = Integer.parseInt(args[++index]);
                }
              }
              case "--stdin-echo" -> {
                if (index + 1 < args.length) {
                  echoClasspath = args[++index];
                }
              }
              case "--terminate-after-stop" -> terminateAfterStop = true;
              default -> {
                // Unknown arguments are ignored so the adapter stays launchable from
                // registry templates that append extra options.
              }
            }
          }
          if (!tcp) {
            new FakeDapServer(System.in, System.out, echoClasspath, terminateAfterStop).serve();
            return;
          }
          try (ServerSocket serverSocket = new ServerSocket(port); Socket socket = serverSocket.accept()) {
            new FakeDapServer(socket.getInputStream(), socket.getOutputStream(), echoClasspath, terminateAfterStop)
              .serve();
          }
        }
      
        private void serve() throws IOException {
          JsonNode message;
          while ((message = readMessage()) != null) {
            if ("request".equals(message.path("type").asText())) {
              handleRequest(message);
            }
            // Responses to requests issued by the client (runInTerminal) need no answer.
          }
          output.flush();
        }
      
        private void handleRequest(JsonNode message) throws IOException {
          String command = message.path("command").asText();
          int requestSequence = message.path("seq").asInt();
          switch (command) {
            case "initialize" -> {
              ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              body.put("supportsConfigurationDoneRequest", true);
              body.put("supportsTerminateRequest", true);
              body.put("supportsRunInTerminalRequest", true);
              respond(requestSequence, command, body);
              event("initialized", MAPPER.createObjectNode());
            }
            case "launch" -> {
              respond(requestSequence, command, null);
              JsonNode arguments = message.path("arguments");
              if (arguments.hasNonNull("mainClass")) {
                publish("{LAUNCH} mainClass=" + arguments.path("mainClass").asText() + " projectName="
                    + arguments.path("projectName").asText());
              }
              if (echoClasspath != null) {
                requestRunInTerminal();
              }
            }
            case "setBreakpoints" -> {
              breakpoints.clear();
              JsonNode requested = message.path("arguments").path("breakpoints");
              ArrayNode verified = MAPPER.createArrayNode();
              int id = 1;
              for (JsonNode breakpoint : requested) {
                int line = breakpoint.path("line").asInt();
                breakpoints.add(line);
                ObjectNode entry = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
                entry.put("id", id++);
                entry.put("verified", true);
                entry.put("line", line);
                verified.add(entry);
              }
              ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              body.set("breakpoints", verified);
              respond(requestSequence, command, body);
              publish("{BREAKPOINTS} " + joinedBreakpoints());
            }
            case "configurationDone" -> {
              respond(requestSequence, command, null);
              publish("{CONFIGURED}");
              stopped("breakpoint");
              if (terminateAfterStop) {
                terminated();
              }
            }
            case "continue" -> {
              ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              body.put("allThreadsContinued", true);
              respond(requestSequence, command, body);
              publish("{CONTROL} continue");
              event("continued", MAPPER.createObjectNode());
              advance();
              stopped(breakpoints.isEmpty() ? "step" : "breakpoint");
            }
            case "next", "stepIn", "stepOut" -> {
              respond(requestSequence, command, null);
              publish("{CONTROL} " + command);
              advance();
              stopped("step");
            }
            case "pause" -> {
              respond(requestSequence, command, null);
              publish("{CONTROL} pause");
              stopped("pause");
            }
            case "threads" -> {
              ObjectNode thread = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              thread.put("id", 1);
              thread.put("name", "main");
              ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              ArrayNode threads = MAPPER.createArrayNode();
              threads.add(thread);
              body.set("threads", threads);
              respond(requestSequence, command, body);
            }
            case "stackTrace" -> {
              ObjectNode frame = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              frame.put("id", 1);
              frame.put("name", "main");
              frame.put("line", currentLine);
              frame.put("column", 1);
              ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
              ArrayNode frames = MAPPER.createArrayNode();
              frames.add(frame);
              body.set("stackFrames", frames);
              body.put("totalFrames", 1);
              respond(requestSequence, command, body);
            }
            case "disconnect" -> {
              respond(requestSequence, command, null);
              terminated();
              output.flush();
              System.exit(0);
            }
            default -> respond(requestSequence, command, null);
          }
        }
      
        private void advance() {
          currentLine++;
        }
      
        private String joinedBreakpoints() {
          StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder();
          for (Integer line : breakpoints) {
            if (text.length() > 0) {
              text.append(',');
            }
            text.append(line);
          }
          return text.toString();
        }
      
        private void requestRunInTerminal() throws IOException {
          String executable = System.getProperty("os.name").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains("win") ? "java.exe"
              : "java";
          String javaExecutable = Path.of(System.getProperty("java.home"), "bin", executable).toString();
          ObjectNode arguments = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          arguments.put("kind", "integrated");
          arguments.put("title", "Echo stdin");
          ArrayNode args = arguments.putArray("args");
          args.add(javaExecutable);
          args.add("-cp");
          args.add(echoClasspath);
          args.add(EchoStdin.class.getName());
      
          ObjectNode request = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          request.put("seq", ++sequence);
          request.put("type", "request");
          request.put("command", "runInTerminal");
          request.set("arguments", arguments);
          send(request);
        }
      
        private void stopped(String reason) throws IOException {
          ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          body.put("reason", reason);
          body.put("threadId", 1);
          body.put("allThreadsStopped", true);
          ObjectNode event = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          event.put("type", "event");
          event.put("event", "stopped");
          event.set("body", body);
          send(event);
        }
      
        private void terminated() throws IOException {
          if (terminatedSent) {
            return;
          }
          terminatedSent = true;
          event("terminated", MAPPER.createObjectNode());
        }
      
        private void publish(String text) throws IOException {
          ObjectNode body = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          body.put("category", "stdout");
          body.put("output", text + "\n");
          event("output", body);
        }
      
        private void event(String name, ObjectNode body) throws IOException {
          ObjectNode node = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          node.put("seq", ++sequence);
          node.put("type", "event");
          node.put("event", name);
          if (body != null && !body.isEmpty()) {
            node.set("body", body);
          }
          send(node);
        }
      
        private void respond(int requestSequence, String command, ObjectNode body) throws IOException {
          ObjectNode node = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
          node.put("seq", ++sequence);
          node.put("type", "response");
          node.put("request_seq", requestSequence);
          node.put("success", true);
          node.put("command", command);
          if (body != null) {
            node.set("body", body);
          }
          send(node);
        }
      
        private void send(JsonNode node) throws IOException {
          byte[] body = MAPPER.writeValueAsString(node).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
          output.write(("Content-Length: " + body.length + "\r\n\r\n").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
          output.write(body);
          output.flush();
        }
      
        private JsonNode readMessage() throws IOException {
          StringBuilder header = new StringBuilder();
          int read;
          while ((read = input.read()) != -1) {
            header.append((char) read);
            if (header.length() >= 4 && header.charAt(header.length() - 4) == '\r'
                && header.charAt(header.length() - 3) == '\n' && header.charAt(header.length() - 2) == '\r'
                && header.charAt(header.length() - 1) == '\n') {
              break;
            }
          }
          if (read == -1) {
            return null;
          }
          int length = contentLength(header.toString());
          if (length < 0) {
            return null;
          }
          byte[] body = input.readNBytes(length);
          if (body.length < length) {
            return null;
          }
          return MAPPER.readTree(body);
        }
      
        private static int contentLength(String header) {
          for (String line : header.split("\r\n")) {
            int colon = line.indexOf(':');
            if (colon > 0 && "content-length".equalsIgnoreCase(line.substring(0, colon).trim())) {
              try {
                return Integer.parseInt(line.substring(colon + 1).trim());
              }
              catch (NumberFormatException error) {
                return -1;
              }
            }
          }
          return -1;
        }
      
      }
      
```

- path: Makefile
  content: |
      ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
      MVNW := mvnw.cmd
      PKG_RUNNER := powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/package.ps1
      else
      MVNW := ./mvnw
      PKG_RUNNER := sh scripts/package.sh
      endif
      
      APP_JAR := simpleide/target/simpleide.jar
      PKG_DIR := simpleide/target/pkg
      VERSION := $(shell sed -n 's/^version=//p' simpleide/src/main/resources/simpleide.properties 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')
      JAVA_OPTS ?= -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED
      
      .PHONY: all build test test-nolang test-debug test-lsp jar pkg pkg-verify change-version run clean format check-format format-check verify help
      
      all: test jar
      
      # Compile every module without running tests or packaging artifacts.
      build:
        $(MVNW) -B -DskipTests compile
      
      # Run the complete test suite.
      test: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -DexcludedGroups=debug test
      
      # Run the test suite without tests that require external language toolchains.
      test-nolang: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -DexcludedGroups=debug,language-tools test
      
      # Run only debug integration tests; the CI workflow supplies the newest toolchains.
      test-debug: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -Dgroups=debug -DexcludedGroups= -Dsimpleide.java.debug.real=true test
      
      # Run only language-server integration tests; the CI workflow supplies the runtime toolchains.
      test-lsp: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -Dgroups=lsp -DexcludedGroups= test
      
      # Package the executable fat JAR. Tests are intentionally not part of this target.
      jar:
        $(MVNW) -B -DskipTests package
        @echo "Fat JAR: $(APP_JAR)"
      
      # Build a self-contained jpackage application image for the current OS/arch.
      # Override with SIMPLEIDE_PKG_TYPE=deb|rpm|dmg|exe|msi|app-image.
      # The Windows .msi is built for x64 only.
      pkg: jar
        $(PKG_RUNNER)
      
      # Validates the packages produced by `make pkg` (zip, installers). Used by CI
      # so a broken executable never reaches a release.
      ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
      PKG_VERIFY := powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/validate-package.ps1
      else
      PKG_VERIFY := sh scripts/validate-package.sh
      endif
      
      pkg-verify: pkg
        $(PKG_VERIFY)
      
      # Changes the project version everywhere it is declared (pom files and the
      # application properties). Requires confirmation; the default answer is NO.
      change-version:
        @sh scripts/change-version.sh "$(VERSAO)"
      
      # Launch the executable fat JAR.
      run: jar
        java $(JAVA_OPTS) -jar "$(APP_JAR)"
      
      # Apply Spring Java Format and the repository's import ordering to every Java source.
      format:
        $(MVNW) -B spring-javaformat:apply
        java scripts/JavaImportFormatter.java --apply
      
      # Fail when Java sources violate Spring Java Format or the repository's import ordering.
      check-format:
        $(MVNW) -B spring-javaformat:validate
        java scripts/JavaImportFormatter.java --check
      
      # Backwards-compatible alias for check-format.
      format-check: check-format
      
      # Full local validation: formatting, tests and packaging.
      verify: check-format test jar
      
      clean:
        $(MVNW) -B clean
        rm -rf "$(PKG_DIR)"
      
      help:
        @echo "Simple IDE build targets"
        @echo ""
        @echo "  make build         Compile all modules (no tests, no packages)"
        @echo "  make test          Run the full test suite"
        @echo "  make test-nolang   Run tests without external language toolchains"
        @echo "  make test-debug    Run only debug integration tests"
        @echo "  make test-lsp      Run only language-server integration tests"
        @echo "  make jar           Package the executable fat JAR"
        @echo "  make pkg           Build every release package for this OS/architecture"
        @echo "  make pkg-verify    Build packages and validate the produced executables"
        @echo "  make change-version VERSION"
        @echo "                     Change the project version (asks for confirmation)"
        @echo "  make run           Launch the executable fat JAR"
        @echo "  make format        Apply Java source and import formatting"
        @echo "  make check-format  Check Java source and import formatting"
        @echo "  make format-check  Alias for check-format"
        @echo "  make verify        Check formatting, run tests and package"
        @echo "  make clean         Remove generated build and package outputs"
        @echo ""
        @echo "Version: $(VERSION)"
        @echo "Fat JAR: $(APP_JAR)"

> _Reasoning_
> Wait: `start()` calls `await(sendBreakpoints(...))` then configurationDone then `await(launchRequest)`. Fine.
> 
> But there's a subtlety: after awaiting launch failure detection, if launch succeeded normally before initialized event (adapter that never sends initialized until much later), we proceed. That matches prior behavior (timeout then proceed).

      package io.simpleide.dap;
      
      import java.io.IOException;
      import java.nio.file.Files;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.ArrayList;
      import java.util.List;
      import java.util.Locale;
      import java.util.Map;
      import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;
      import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;
      
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.io.Input;
      import io.simpleide.language.io.Output;
      
      /**
       * Integration tests that start a real debug adapter process and drive a full debug
       * session over the Debug Adapter Protocol.
       *
       * <p>
       * The adapter is {@link FakeDapServer} launched as a child process, so the tests exercise
       * the real framing, the real sockets and pipes, the breakpoint handshake and every
       * execution control exposed by the IDE. The adapter echoes each control request it
       * receives, which lets the test assert that the command really travelled over the wire.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      @Tag("debug")
      class DapSessionIntegrationTest {
      
        private static final List<String> TRANSPORTS = List.of("stdio", "tcp");
      
        @TempDir
        Path tempDirectory;
      
        private final List<String> published = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
      
        private final List<String> listenerEvents = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
      
        private AutoCloseable outputSubscription;
      
        @BeforeEach
        void subscribeToOutput() throws InterruptedException {
          while (Input.getInstance().get(0) != null) {
            // Drain input left by other tests.
          }
          published.clear();
          listenerEvents.clear();
          outputSubscription = Output.getInstance()
            .addListener(line -> published.add("[" + line.type() + "] " + line.text()));
        }
      
        @AfterEach
        void unsubscribeFromOutput() throws Exception {
          outputSubscription.close();
        }
      
        @Test
        void completesHandshakeAndReportsBreakpointsOverStdio() throws Exception {
          runSession("stdio", List.of(1, 2));
        }
      
        @Test
        void completesHandshakeAndReportsBreakpointsOverTcp() throws Exception {
          runSession("tcp", List.of(7, 9));
        }
      
        private void runSession(String transport, List<Integer> lines) throws Exception {
          DapSession session = new DapSession(adapter(transport, true), tempDirectory, program(), listener());
          try {
            session.start(lines);
      
            assertThat(session.supportsConfigurationDone()).isTrue();
            awaitOutput("[OUTPUT] " + Output.INITIALIZED);
            awaitOutput("{BREAKPOINTS} " + join(lines));
            await().atMost(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
              .untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(listenerEvents).contains("stopped:breakpoint", "terminated"));
            awaitOutput("[OUTPUT] " + Output.FINISHED);
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
        }
      
        @Test
        void drivesEveryExecutionControlOverTheWire() throws Exception {
          DapSession session = new DapSession(adapter("stdio", false), tempDirectory, program(), listener());
          try {
            session.start(List.of(1));
            await().atMost(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
              .untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(listenerEvents).contains("stopped:breakpoint"));
      
            session.stepOver();
            awaitOutput("{CONTROL} next");
      
            session.stepInto();
            awaitOutput("{CONTROL} stepIn");
      
            session.stepOut();
            awaitOutput("{CONTROL} stepOut");
      
            session.pause();
            awaitOutput("{CONTROL} pause");
      
            session.resume();
            awaitOutput("{CONTROL} continue");
            await().atMost(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(listenerEvents).contains("continued"));
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
        }
      
        @Test
        void sendsUpdatedBreakpointsWhileTheSessionIsRunning() throws Exception {
          DapSession session = new DapSession(adapter("tcp", false), tempDirectory, program(), listener());
          try {
            session.start(List.of(1));
            awaitOutput("{BREAKPOINTS} 1");
      
            session.setBreakpoints(program(), List.of(4, 8));
            awaitOutput("{BREAKPOINTS} 4,8");
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
        }
      
        @Test
        void forwardsTypedInputToTheLiveDebuggee() throws Exception {
          DapSession session = new DapSession(adapterWithStdinEcho(), tempDirectory, program(), listener());
          try {
            session.start(List.of(1));
      
            awaitOutput("[OUTPUT] " + Output.WAITING_FOR_STDIN);
      
            Input.getInstance().set("hello from the test");
            awaitOutput("ECHO: hello from the test");
      
            Input.getInstance().set("quit");
            awaitOutput("ECHO: quit");
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
          await().atMost(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(listenerEvents).contains("terminated"));
          awaitOutput("[OUTPUT] " + Output.FINISHED);
        }
      
        @Test
        void reportsAnUnlaunchableAdapterAsIOException() throws Exception {
          DapAdapter adapter = new DapAdapter("missing", "Missing adapter", "1.0.0", "missing",
              List.of("this-command-does-not-exist"), List.of(), "stdio", Map.of(), Map.of());
          DapSession session = new DapSession(adapter, tempDirectory, program(), listener());
          try {
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> session.start(List.of())).isInstanceOf(IOException.class)
              .hasMessageContaining("missing");
          }
          finally {
            session.close();
          }
        }
      
        private void awaitOutput(String fragment) {
          await().atMost(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(published).as("output lines").anyMatch(line -> line.contains(fragment)));
        }
      
        private DapAdapter adapter(String transport, boolean terminateAfterStop) {
          List<String> arguments = new ArrayList<>(List.of("-cp", classpath(), FakeDapServer.class.getName()));
          if (transport.equals("tcp")) {
            arguments.add("tcp");
            arguments.add("${port}");
          }
          if (terminateAfterStop) {
            arguments.add("--terminate-after-stop");
          }
          return new DapAdapter("fake", "Fake debug adapter", "1.0.0", "fake", javaExecutable(), arguments, List.of(),
              transport, Map.of(), Map.of());
        }
      
        private DapAdapter adapterWithStdinEcho() {
          return new DapAdapter("fake", "Fake debug adapter", "1.0.0", "fake", javaExecutable(),
              List.of("-cp", classpath(), FakeDapServer.class.getName(), "--stdin-echo", classpath()), List.of(),
              "stdio", Map.of(), Map.of());
        }
      
        private Path program() throws IOException {
          Path program = tempDirectory.resolve("program.txt");
          if (!Files.exists(program)) {
            Files.writeString(program, "line one\nline two\nline three\nline four\n");
          }
          return program;
        }
      
        private DapSession.Listener listener() {
          return new DapSession.Listener() {
            @Override
            public void onStopped(int threadId, String reason) {
              listenerEvents.add("stopped:" + reason);
            }
      
            @Override
            public void onContinued() {
              listenerEvents.add("continued");
            }
      
            @Override
            public void onTerminated() {
              listenerEvents.add("terminated");
            }
          };
        }
      
        private static String join(List<Integer> lines) {
          StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder();
          for (Integer line : lines) {
            if (text.length() > 0) {
              text.append(',');
            }
            text.append(line);
          }
          return text.toString();
        }
      
        private static String javaExecutable() {
          String executable = System.getProperty("os.name").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains("win") ? "java.exe"
              : "java";
          return Path.of(System.getProperty("java.home"), "bin", executable).toString();
        }
      
        private static String classpath() {
          return System.getProperty("java.class.path");
        }
      
      }

package io.simpleide.thread;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;

import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

import io.simpleide.thread.nodes.NodePattern;

/**
 * Process-wide thread manager shared by the application and its subsystems.
 *
 * <p>
 * The singleton is created on demand by {@link #getInstance()} and rooted at a node with
 * level zero that executes on the Swing Event Dispatch Thread. Use the inherited methods
 * to register nodes, run a task on the EDT or a background pool, schedule a delayed task
 * and shut the manager down. The simpler facade used by most embedding applications is
 * {@code io.simpleide.api.Threads}.
 *
 * <p>
 * Covered by {@code ThreadMasterTest}.
 *
 * @author BrunoRNS
 * @since v1.0.0beta
 * @see <a href=
 * "https://github.com/BrunoRNS/SIMPLE-IDE/blob/main/docs/api/threading.md">docs/api/threading.md</a>
 */
public final class ThreadMaster extends AbstractThreadMaster {

  private static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger(ThreadMaster.class);

  private final NodePattern root;

  private final List<NamedShutdownAction> shutdownActions = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();

  private final AtomicBoolean shutdownHookInstalled = new AtomicBoolean();

  public ThreadMaster(NodePattern root) {
    super(root);
    this.root = root;
  }

  /**
   * Returns the root pattern of the thread tree.
   * @return the root node, which runs on the EDT at level zero
   */
  public NodePattern getROOT() {
    return root;
  }

  /**
   * Registers an action that runs once when the JVM shuts down.
   *
   * <p>
   * The shutdown hook thread is created here, inside the thread manager, so application
   * code never creates its own thread. Actions are executed in registration order and a
   * failing action does not prevent the remaining actions from running.
   * @param name descriptive action name used in log messages
   * @param action action to execute during shutdown, must not be {@code null}
   */
  public void registerShutdownAction(String name, Runnable action) {
    if (action == null) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Shutdown action must not be null.");
    }
    String actionName = name == null || name.isBlank() ? "unnamed" : name;
    shutdownActions.add(new NamedShutdownAction(actionName, action));
    if (shutdownHookInstalled.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
      Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(this::runShutdownActions, "simpleide-shutdown"));
    }
  }

  private void runShutdownActions() {
    for (NamedShutdownAction shutdownAction : shutdownActions) {
      try {
        shutdownAction.action().run();
      }
      catch (RuntimeException error) {
        LOGGER.warn("Shutdown action '{}' failed.", shutdownAction.name(), error);
      }
    }
  }

  private record NamedShutdownAction(String name, Runnable action) {
  }

  /**
   * Returns the shared thread manager, creating it on first use.
   * @return the process-wide {@code ThreadMaster}
   */
  public static ThreadMaster getInstance() {
    return ThreadMasterHolder.INSTANCE;
  }

}

      package io.simpleide.thread.nodes.runnable;
      
      import io.simpleide.thread.ThreadMaster;
      import io.simpleide.thread.nodes.Node;
      import io.simpleide.thread.nodes.NodePattern;
      
      /**
       * Thread tree node that executes on a managed background worker.
       *
       * <p>
       * Unlike {@link io.simpleide.thread.nodes.edt.EDTNode}, this node reports {@code false}
       * from {@link #isEDT()} and derives its level from the parent node. It is the standard
       * type for tasks registered on the shared worker pool.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.0.0beta
       */
      public class RunnableNode extends Node {
      
        public RunnableNode(NodePattern superNode, NodePattern actual) {
          super(superNode, actual);
        }
      
        public RunnableNode(NodePattern superNode, Runnable onStart) {
          super(superNode, onStart);
        }
      
        public RunnableNode(NodePattern superNode, Runnable onStart, Runnable onClose) {
          super(superNode, onStart, onClose);
        }
      
        public RunnableNode(NodePattern actual) {
          super(ThreadMaster.getInstance().getROOT(), actual);
        }
      
        public RunnableNode(Runnable onStart) {
          super(ThreadMaster.getInstance().getROOT(), onStart);
        }
      
        public RunnableNode(Runnable onStart, Runnable onClose) {
          super(ThreadMaster.getInstance().getROOT(), onStart, onClose);
        }
      
        @Override
        public Runnable onStart() {
          return this.start;
        }
      
        @Override
        public Runnable onClose() {
          return this.close;
        }
      
        @Override
        public Integer level() {
          return this.superNode.level() + 1;
        }
      
        @Override
        public boolean isEDT() {
          return false;
        }
      
      }

the test presses the same\n * button the user does and checks that the process is killed, that the language reports\n * the manual interruption and that the panel returns to its idle state.\n *\n * @author BrunoRNS\n * @since v1.1.0\n */\nclass IOPanelRunStopIntegrationTest {\n\n\t@Test\n\tvoid stopsAProgramRunningWithoutDebugging() throws Exception {\n\t\tdrainInput();\n\t\tIOPanel panel = new IOPanel();\n\t\tRunningLanguage language = new RunningLanguage();\n\t\tpanel.beginRun(language);\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tlanguage.startManaged();\n\t\t\tawait().atMost(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)\n\t\t\t\t.untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(panel.getOutputText()).contains(\"PROBE started\"));\n\t\t\tassertThat(panel.getRunControls().isVisible()).isTrue();\n\n\t\t\tJButton stop = (JButton) panel.getRunControls().getComponent(0);\n\t\t\tSwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(stop::doClick);\n\n\t\t\tawait().atMost(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)\n\t\t\t\t.untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isFalse());\n\t\t\tassertThat(panel.getOutputText()).contains(\"Process interrupted by the user.\");\n\t\t\tassertThat(panel.getRunControls().isVisible()).isFalse();\n\t\t}\n\t\tfinally {\n\t\t\tlanguage.forceStop();\n\t\t\tpanel.finishExecution();\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tprivate static void drainInput() throws InterruptedException {\n\t\twhile (Input.getInstance().get(0) != null) {\n\t\t\t// Drain input left by other tests.\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tprivate static String javaExecutable() {\n\t\tString executable = System.getProperty(\"os.name\").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains(\"win\") ? \"java.exe\"\n\t\t\t\t: \"java\";\n\t\treturn Path.of(System.getProperty(\"java.home\"), \"bin\", executable).toString();\n\t}\n\n\tprivate static final class RunningLanguage extends AbstractLanguage {\n\n\t\tprivate RunningLanguage() {\n\t\t\tpb = new ProcessBuilder(javaExecutable(), \"-cp\", System.getProperty(\"java.class.path\"),\n\t\t\t\t\tRunStopProbe.class.getName());\n\t\t}\n\n\t}\n\n}\n"

  "command": "cd simpleide/src/main/resources/io/simpleide/dap && python3 - <<'EOF'\nimport json\n\ndef dump(value, indent=0, inline_ok=False):\n    pad = \"  \" * indent\n    inner = \"  \" * (indent + 1)\n    if isinstance(value, dict):\n        if not value:\n            return \"{}\"\n        if inline_ok and all(not isinstance(v, (dict, list)) for v in value.values()):\n            return \"{ \" + \", \".join(f'\"{k}\": {json.dumps(v)}' for k, v in value.items()) + \" }\"\n        lines = [pad + \"{\"]\n        items = list(value.items())\n        for index, (k, v) in enumerate(items):\n            comma = \",\" if index < len(items) - 1 else \"\"\n            lines.append(inner + json.dumps(k) + \": \" + dump(v, indent + 1).lstrip() + comma)\n        lines.append(pad + \"}\")\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n    if isinstance(value, list):\n        if not value:\n            return \"[]\"\n        lines = [pad + \"[\"]\n        for index, v in enumerate(value):\n            comma = \",\" if index < len(value) - 1 else \"\"\n            lines.append(inner + dump(v, indent + 1, inline_ok=True).lstrip() + comma)\n        lines.append(pad + \"]\")\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n    return json.dumps(value)\n\nfor name in (\"registry.json\", \"dap_registry.json\"):\n    data = json.load(open(name))\n    open(name, \"w\").write(dump(data) + \"\\n\")\nEOF\ngit diff --stat .; diff registry.json dap_registry.json && echo IDENTICAL; git diff registry.json",

- path: docs/reference/DAP.md
  content: |
      # Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP)
      
      Simple IDE supports interactive debugging through the Debug Adapter Protocol.
      Adapters are either external processes that speak DAP over standard
      input/output or TCP, or a debug server hosted by a language server. The supported
      adapter definitions and their per-platform download metadata live in
      [`simpleide/src/main/resources/io/simpleide/dap/registry.json`](../../simpleide/src/main/resources/io/simpleide/dap/registry.json)
      (mirrored as `dap_registry.json`).
      
      Debugging is available for **JavaScript, Python, Go and Java**. Opening another
      file type and invoking Debug reports that the language is not debuggable; it does
      not disable debugging for the supported languages.
      
      ## Components
      
      | Type | Responsibility |
      | --- | --- |
      | `DapRegistry` | Parses the bundled registry and matches adapters to the host platform |
      | `DapAdapter` | Adapter command, arguments, transport, launch properties and downloads |
      | `DapDownload` | Download URL and archive type for one OS/architecture pair |
      | `DapInstaller` | Downloads, extracts and marks an adapter under `~/.simpleide/dap` |
      | `DapManager` | Resolves, installs and starts a session for a source file |
      | `DapSession` | Connects to the adapter, sends `initialize`/`launch` and exposes execution controls |
      | `JavaDebugBridge` | Drives the Java debug server hosted by the JDT language server |
      
      ## Registry
      
      Each adapter declares an id, name, version, language id, launch command, transport
      (`stdio`, `tcp` or `jdtls`), optional launch properties and a download entry per
      platform:
      
      ```json
      {
        "adapters": [
          {
            "id": "js-debug",
            "name": "JavaScript Debug Adapter",
            "version": "1.140.1",
            "languageId": "javascript",
            "command": "node",
            "transport": "tcp",
            "launch": { "type": "pwa-node", "console": "internalConsole" },
            "arguments": ["${installDir}/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js", "${port}"],
            "downloads": [
              { "os": "linux", "arch": "x64", "url": "https://example.com/js-debug.tar.gz", "archiveType": "tar.gz" }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
      ```
      
      Command arguments support `${installDir}`, `${program}` and `${port}`; launch
      property strings support `${program}` and `${fileDir}`. Launch values may also be
      booleans or numbers (for example Python's `justMyCode: false`), and they are sent
      to the adapter with their JSON type preserved. Platform matching uses
      `LangPlatform` values: `windows`, `linux` or `macos` combined with `x86`, `x64`,
      `arm64` or `aarch64`; `amd64` is accepted as an alias of `x64`.
      
      ## Transports per language
      
      | Language | Adapter | Transport | How it starts |
      | --- | --- | --- | --- |
      | JavaScript | `js-debug` | `tcp` | IDE picks a free port and passes it as an argument |
      | Python | `debugpy` | `tcp` | `python3 -m debugpy --listen 127.0.0.1:${port}`; uses `console: integratedTerminal` so `input()` is forwarded through the I/O tab, and `justMyCode: false` so stepping enters library code |
      | Go | `delve` | `tcp` | `dlv dap --listen 127.0.0.1:${port}`; launches with `mode: debug` and the source file, so standalone files without a `go.mod` work |
      | Java | `vscode-java-debug` in JDT LS | `jdtls` | Language server command, no download |
      
      Adapters that speak DAP on their standard input/output use the `stdio` transport.
      Server-style adapters bind different loopback addresses: `debugpy` and `delve`
      listen on IPv4 while the JavaScript adapter listens on IPv6, and the IDE tries
      both `127.0.0.1` and `::1` when connecting.
      
      ## Child debug sessions
      
      The JavaScript adapter launches the program as a nested session: after `launch` it
      sends a `startDebugging` request and expects the IDE to open the child session.
      `DapSession` opens that child session on the same adapter port, inherits the
      breakpoints and forwards its events, and execution controls follow the session
      that actually stopped. Thread identifier `0` is accepted, and the `initialized`
      event is awaited for at most 90 seconds so adapters that build the program first,
      like delve, still start.
      
      ## Installing and launching
      
      `DapManager.createDefault()` reads the bundled registry and detects the current
      platform. `isSupported()` reports whether an adapter exists; `prepare()`
      downloads and extracts it when no matching `.installed` marker is present.
      Downloads must use HTTPS and are removed when extraction fails, so a failed
      attempt never leaves a partial installation behind.
      
      Sessions always start the program with a `launch` request; `attach` is never used.
      The adapter's `runInTerminal` request starts the debuggee with its standard
      input, output and error streams connected to the I/O tab through the shared
      `Input` and `Output` APIs. For an unknown platform, missing download, or failed
      installation, `DapManager.DapUnavailableException` carries a user-facing message
      that `MainFrame` shows to the user.
      
      ## Java through the JDT language server
      
      Java debugging runs inside Eclipse JDT LS instead of a downloaded adapter:
      
      1. `vscode.java.startDebugSession` starts the debug server and returns its port.
      2. `vscode.java.resolveMainClass` resolves the main class of the open file.
      3. `vscode.java.resolveClasspath` returns the module and class paths.
      4. `DapSession` connects over TCP and sends `launch` with `mainClass`,
         `projectName`, `modulePaths`, `classPaths`, `cwd` and `console`.
      
      The language server already connected to the editor tab is reused; when the tab
      has none yet, `EditorManager.connectLanguageServer` connects one. Java debugging
      therefore requires an Eclipse JDT language server with the `vscode-java-debug`
      plugin loaded. Without it the commands are not registered and the IDE reports
      that the language server rejected the command. The IDE downloads the
      `vscode-java-debug` bundle and passes it to the server in
      `initializationOptions.bundles`; the language server itself still has to be
      available.
      
      ### Files outside a project
      
      JDT LS does not report a main class for a loose `.java` file, because the file is
      not part of any project and nothing compiles it. A Run/Debug request for such a
      file therefore compiles the file with the JDK compiler into a temporary
      directory, picks the compiled class named like the file (or the first top-level
      class), and sends that directory as the only `classPaths` entry. If the file does
      not compile, the IDE reports the failure instead of launching a class that does
      not exist.
      
      ## Breakpoints
      
      Breakpoints are stored per editor in `Editor` and painted in the gutter icon
      column through `Gutter.addLineTrackingIcon`. They are visible for every supported
      language file.
      
      - Clicking the gutter toggles the breakpoint on the clicked line. The breakpoint
        column is the gutter's icon row header, which is a child component, so the
        mouse listeners are installed on the gutter and on its children.
      - The hovered line shows a translucent dot preview; selected lines show a solid
        red dot.
      - Toggling a breakpoint (F9 or gutter click) notifies the active `DapSession`
        through `setBreakpoints`, so the adapter always receives the current line set
        for the debugged file.
      
      ## Output and controls
      
      Adapter and debuggee output events are published to the shared `Output` queue, so
      the I/O tab renders them with the same `[OUTPUT]`, `[ERROR]` and `[DEBUG]`
      colours as normal program output. Session milestones appear as `[OUTPUT]`
      markers:
      
      | Marker | Meaning |
      | --- | --- |
      | `[OUTPUT] {INITIALIZED}` | The adapter completed the DAP handshake |
      | `[OUTPUT] {WAITING FOR STDIN}` | The debuggee is running and waiting for input; repeated after each forwarded line |
      | `[OUTPUT] {FINISHED}` | The session terminated or the user stopped it |
      
      `DapSession` sends `setBreakpoints` for the selected file and exposes `resume`,
      `pause`, `stepOver`, `stepInto`, `stepOut` and `close`, which back the debug
      buttons shown by `IOPanel` while a debug session is active. Step requests are
      ignored while the program is running; the I/O tab prints that execution is
      running.
      
      ## Tests
      
      - `DapRegistryTest` covers registry parsing, platform/architecture matching,
        command placeholders and bundled downloads.
      - `DapRegistryIntegrationTest` covers that every supported platform resolves to
        an adapter and that every adapter ships downloads for all OS/architecture
        combinations.
      - `DapLanguageRegistryTest` covers the four debuggable languages, transports,
        language mapping and that language-server adapters are never installed.
      - `DapManagerTest` covers unsupported-platform fallback without network access.
      - `DapInstallerTest` covers installed-version markers and cleanup after a
        rejected insecure download.
      - `DapSessionIntegrationTest` starts a real adapter process over `stdio` and
        `tcp` and exercises the whole session, including the execution controls and the
        output markers.
      - `DapIOPanelIntegrationTest` clicks every debug button against a live adapter.
      - `JavaDebugBridgeIntegrationTest` runs the Java path against a real TCP adapter
        and a stubbed language-server client, including the loose-file compilation
        fallback and its compile-error message.
      - `JavaRealDebugIntegrationTest` debugs a real loose `Main.java` through JDT LS:
        it stops at a breakpoint, resumes and checks the program output. It is skipped
        unless the build enables it with `-Dsimpleide.java.debug.real=true`, which
        `make test-debug` does.
      - `JsDebugAdapterIntegrationTest` debugs a real Node.js program with the installed
        `js-debug` adapter (tagged `language-tools`, skipped without `node`, without the
        adapter, or on an operating system and architecture with no registered adapter).
      - `IOPanelTest` and `InputForwarderTest` cover output colouring, input forwarding
        and debug-mode controls.
      
- path: docs/api/dap.md
  content: |
      # Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP)
      
      `io.simpleide.dap` adds debug support to the Execute menu. It uses the Eclipse
      LSP4J debug protocol client (`org.eclipse.lsp4j:org.eclipse.lsp4j.debug`) and the
      Debug Adapter Protocol, so adapters are either ordinary external processes that
      speak DAP over standard input/output or TCP, or a debug server hosted by a
      language server.
      
      Debugging is offered for **JavaScript, Python, Go and Java** only. Any other file
      reports a short message when Debug is invoked and leaves debugging enabled for
      the supported languages.
      
      ## Components
      
      | Type | Responsibility |
      | --- | --- |
      | `DapRegistry` | Parses the bundled `registry.json` and matches adapters to the host platform |
      | `DapAdapter` | Adapter command, arguments, transport, launch properties and downloads |
      | `DapDownload` | Download URL and archive type for one OS/architecture pair |
      | `DapInstaller` | Downloads, extracts and marks an adapter under `~/.simpleide/dap` |
      | `DapManager` | Resolves, installs and starts a session for a source file |
      | `DapSession` | Connects to the adapter, sends `initialize`/`launch` and exposes execution controls |
      | `JavaDebugBridge` | Drives the Java debug server hosted by the JDT language server |
      
      The registry lives at
      `simpleide/src/main/resources/io/simpleide/dap/registry.json` (mirrored as
      `dap_registry.json`). Each adapter has an id, name, version, language id, launch
      command, transport, optional launch properties and a download entry per platform:
      
      ```json
      {
        "adapters": [
          {
            "id": "js-debug",
            "name": "JavaScript Debug Adapter",
            "version": "1.140.1",
            "languageId": "javascript",
            "command": "node",
            "transport": "tcp",
            "launch": { "type": "pwa-node", "console": "internalConsole" },
            "arguments": ["${installDir}/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js", "${port}"],
            "downloads": [
              {
                "os": "linux",
                "arch": "x64",
                "url": "https://example.com/js-debug.tar.gz",
                "archiveType": "tar.gz"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
      ```
      
      Command arguments support `${installDir}`, `${program}` and `${port}`, and launch
      property strings support `${program}` and `${fileDir}`. Launch values may also be
      booleans or numbers (for example Python's `justMyCode: false`) and keep their JSON
      type in the `launch` request. Platform matching uses
      `LangPlatform` values: `windows`, `linux` or `macos` combined with `x86`, `x64`,
      `arm64` or `aarch64`; `amd64` is accepted as an alias of `x64`.
      
      ## Transports per language
      
      | Language | Adapter | Transport | Notes |
      | --- | --- | --- | --- |
      | JavaScript | `js-debug` (`js-debug-dap`) | `tcp` | The IDE picks a free port and passes it as the last argument |
      | Python | `debugpy` | `tcp` | Started with `-m debugpy --listen 127.0.0.1:${port}`; `console: integratedTerminal` forwards `input()` through the I/O tab and `justMyCode: false` allows stepping into library code |
      | Go | `delve` (`dlv dap`) | `tcp` | Launches with `mode: debug` and the source file, so standalone files without a `go.mod` work |
      | Java | `vscode-java-debug` inside JDT LS | `jdtls` | Reached through the language server, nothing is downloaded by the IDE |
      
      `stdio` remains supported by `DapSession` and is used by adapters that read and
      write DAP on their standard input/output.
      
      Server-style adapters bind different loopback addresses: `debugpy` and `delve`
      listen on IPv4, while the JavaScript adapter listens on IPv6. `DapSession` tries
      `127.0.0.1` and then `::1` on every connection attempt, so all three work
      without extra configuration.
      
      ## Child debug sessions
      
      Adapters may launch the debuggee as a nested session. The JavaScript adapter does
      this: after `launch` it sends a `startDebugging` reverse request whose
      configuration identifies a pending runtime target, and the IDE must open a second
      session for it. `DapSession` handles the request by opening a child session on the
      same adapter port, inheriting the current breakpoints and forwarding events to the
      same listener. Execution controls follow the session that actually stopped, so
      `resume`, `pause` and the step commands reach the child while it is paused and
      return to the parent when it continues or terminates.
      
      Adapters that do not report a thread on `stopped` are queried with `threads`
      before a control request is sent. Thread identifier `0` is treated as a valid
      thread, because the JavaScript adapter uses it. The `initialized` event is awaited
      for at most 90 seconds before `launch`, so adapters such as delve that build the
      program first still start correctly.
      
      ## Installing and launching
      
      `DapManager.createDefault()` reads the bundled registry and detects the current
      platform. `isSupported()` reports whether an adapter exists; `prepare()` installs
      an adapter that is downloaded as a process. Downloads must use HTTPS and are
      removed when extraction fails, so a failed attempt never leaves a partial
      installation behind.
      
      ### Facade
      
      `io.simpleide.api.Debugger` starts standalone adapters and Java sessions through
      the language server without exposing the registry and installer details.
      
      ```java
      import io.simpleide.api.Debugger;
      import io.simpleide.dap.DapSession;
      import io.simpleide.lsp.client.LspClient;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.List;
      
      Path program = Path.of("src/main.py");
      if (Debugger.isSupported(program)) {
        DapSession session =
            Debugger.start(program, List.of(12), new DapSession.Listener() { });
        session.close();
      }
      
      // Java is debugged through an initialized JDT language server.
      LspClient javaServer = /* client from LanguageServers.connect(...) */ null;
      DapSession javaSession =
          Debugger.startJava(Path.of("src/Main.java"), javaServer, List.of(4), null);
      ```
      
      `Debugger.languageOf(Path)` returns the language used to select an adapter and
      `Debugger.isLanguageServerDebug(Path)` reports whether the file uses the
      `jdtls` transport.
      
      ### Lower-level manager
      
      ```java
      DapManager manager = DapManager.createDefault();
      if (manager.supports(Path.of("src/main.js"))) {
        DapSession session = manager.start(
            Path.of("src/main.js"),
            List.of(12, 20),
            new DapSession.Listener() {
              @Override
              public void onStopped(int threadId, String reason) {
                System.out.println("stopped: " + reason);
              }
            });
        // session.resume(), session.stepOver(), session.close()
      }
      ```
      
      Sessions always start the program with a `launch` request; `attach` is never
      used. The adapter's `runInTerminal` request starts the debuggee with its standard
      input, output and error streams connected to the I/O tab through the shared
      `Input` and `Output` APIs. For an unknown platform, missing download, or failed
      installation, `DapManager.DapUnavailableException` carries a user-facing message.
      `MainFrame` shows that message and keeps debugging available for the other
      languages.
      
      `DapManager.start` refuses adapters whose transport is `jdtls`, because there is
      no standalone process to launch; use `startJava` for those.
      
      ## Java through the JDT language server
      
      The Java debug adapter is hosted by Eclipse JDT LS, so the IDE never downloads or
      launches it. `JavaDebugBridge` uses the workspace commands the language server
      exposes and then opens a `DapSession` over TCP on the returned port:
      
      1. `vscode.java.startDebugSession` starts the debug server and returns its port.
      2. `vscode.java.resolveMainClass` resolves the main class of the open file; the
         entry whose simple name matches the file name is preferred, otherwise the
         first one is used.
      3. `vscode.java.resolveClasspath` returns `[modulePaths, classPaths]`, which are
         forwarded to the adapter.
      4. The DAP `launch` request carries `mainClass`, `projectName`, `modulePaths`,
         `classPaths`, `cwd`, `name` and `console: internalConsole`.
      
      ### Loose Java files
      
      A Java file outside any project has no JDT build output, and
      `vscode.java.resolveMainClass` returns an empty list for it. Launching the file
      name anyway used to start a class that did not exist. `JavaDebugBridge` now
      handles that case itself:
      
      1. The file is compiled with the JDK compiler into a temporary directory
         (`simpleide-java-debug-*` under the system temporary directory).
      2. The main class is the compiled class whose simple name matches the file name,
         falling back to the first top-level class the compiler produced.
      3. `classPaths` contains only that output directory, so the adapter runs the
         freshly compiled bytecode.
      
      When no compiler is available or the file does not compile, the session is not
      started and the error names the file, so a syntax error is reported before DAP
      instead of failing inside a debuggee that cannot be found.
      
      ```java
      JavaDebugClient client = (command, arguments) -> lspClient.executeCommand(command, arguments);
      DapSession session = manager.startJava(Path.of("src/App.java"), client, List.of(10), listener);
      ```
      
      `MainFrame` reuses the language server already connected to the tab, connecting
      one when the tab has none yet. When the language server fails a command, the
      session is not started and the error message names the failing step.
      
      ### Requirements
      
      Java debugging requires an Eclipse JDT language server that has the
      `vscode-java-debug` plugin loaded; otherwise `vscode.java.startDebugSession` is
      not registered and the IDE reports that the language server rejected the
      command. `LanguageServerManager` downloads the newest compatible
      `vscode-java-debug` bundle with `JavaDebugInstaller` and passes it to JDT LS in
      its `initializationOptions.bundles`, so only the language server itself has to be
      available. The full path, including a loose file without a project, is exercised
      by `JavaRealDebugIntegrationTest` (tagged `language-tools` and `debug`, enabled
      with `-Dsimpleide.java.debug.real=true`).
      
      ## Breakpoints
      
      Breakpoints are stored per editor in `Editor` and painted in the gutter icon
      column through `Gutter.addLineTrackingIcon`:
      
      - Clicking any part of the gutter toggles the breakpoint of the clicked line.
        The breakpoint column is drawn by the gutter's icon row header, a child
        component, so `EditorTab` installs the mouse listeners on the gutter and on all
        of its children.
      - The line under the pointer shows a translucent dot as a preview; a selected
        line shows a solid red dot.
      - F9 toggles a breakpoint on the caret line.
      - Every toggle notifies the listener registered with
        `Editor.setBreakpointListener(Consumer<List<Integer>>)`, which `MainFrame`
        wires to `DapSession.setBreakpoints`, so the adapter receives the current line
        set for the debugged file.
      
      ## Output and controls
      
      Adapter and debuggee output is published to the shared `Output` queue, so the I/O
      tab renders it with the same `[OUTPUT]`, `[ERROR]` and `[DEBUG]` prefixes as
      normal program output. Session milestones are published as `[OUTPUT]` markers so
      the user can follow the handshake:
      
      | Marker | Published when |
      | --- | --- |
      | `[OUTPUT] {INITIALIZED}` | The adapter answered the DAP handshake with its `initialized` event |
      | `[OUTPUT] {WAITING FOR STDIN}` | The debuggee is running and its input is open, once after launch and again after each forwarded line |
      | `[OUTPUT] {FINISHED}` | The adapter reported `terminated`, or the session was closed by the user |
      
      `DapSession` exposes `resume`, `pause`, `stepOver`, `stepInto`, `stepOut` and
      `close`, which back the debug buttons shown by `IOPanel` while a debug session is
      active. Stepping requests are only sent while the adapter reported a stopped
      state; otherwise the I/O tab prints that execution is running.
      
      ## Tests
      
      - `DapRegistryTest` covers registry parsing, platform/architecture matching,
        command placeholders and bundled downloads.
      - `DapRegistryIntegrationTest` covers that every supported platform resolves to
        an adapter and that every adapter ships downloads for all OS/architecture
        combinations.
      - `DapLanguageRegistryTest` covers the four debuggable languages, their
        transports, source-file language mapping and that language-server adapters are
        never installed as processes.
      - `DapManagerTest` covers unsupported-platform fallback without network access.
      - `DapInstallerTest` covers installed-version markers and cleanup after a rejected
        insecure download.
      - `DapSessionIntegrationTest` starts a real adapter process over `stdio` and
        `tcp` and drives the full session: `initialize`, `launch`,
        `setBreakpoints`/`configurationDone`, `continue`, `next`, `stepIn`, `stepOut`,
        `pause`, breakpoint updates during a session, typed standard input reaching the
        live debuggee, and the `{INITIALIZED}`/`{WAITING FOR STDIN}`/`{FINISHED}`
        markers.
      - `DapIOPanelIntegrationTest` clicks every debug button in the I/O tab against a
        live adapter and checks the adapter received the matching request.
      - `JavaDebugBridgeIntegrationTest` runs the Java path end to end against a real
        TCP adapter and a stubbed language-server client, asserting the command
        sequence, the `mainClass`/`projectName` launch properties, breakpoints and
        execution controls. It also covers a loose file (compiled into a temporary
        directory, launched by its compiled class name) and a loose file that fails to
        compile.
      - `JavaRealDebugIntegrationTest` starts the real JDT language server with the
        downloaded debug bundle, stops at a breakpoint in a loose `Main.java` outside
        any project, resumes and checks the program output. `make test-debug` enables
        it with `-Dsimpleide.java.debug.real=true`.
      - `JsDebugAdapterIntegrationTest` debugs a real Node.js program with the installed
        `js-debug` adapter: it stops at a breakpoint, steps over, resumes and checks the
        program output. The test is tagged `language-tools` and skipped when the current
        operating system and architecture have no registered adapter, when the adapter
        is not installed, or when `node` is missing, so `make test-nolang` and headless
        CI images without the external JavaScript toolchain still pass.
      - `IOPanelTest` and `InputForwarderTest` cover output colouring, input forwarding
        and debug-mode controls.
      
````

> _Reasoning_
> Good. One concern: `CompletableFuture.anyOf(initialized, launchRequest)` — if `initialized` completes exceptionally (never does) fine.
> 
> Also: if the launch succeeds immediately but initialized never arrives (some adapters), anyOf resolves on launch and we continue — correct.
> 
> Edge: if launch fails but initialized completed earlier, we still throw the launch failure. Good — that's desired (the error from delve arrives as launch failure; but note delve sends initialized only after successful launch, so no conflict).
> 
> Also `java.util.concurrent.CompletionException` fully-qualified while other imports exist; formatter accepted. Could import it for cleanliness. Let's import CompletionException at top (java.util.concurrent.*) — there's already imports of CompletableFuture, CopyOnWriteArrayList, ExecutionException, TimeUnit, TimeoutException, AtomicBoolean, AtomicReference. Add import java.util.concurrent.CompletionException; and use simple name. Cleaner.

Os três pontos estão resolvidos. O debug de Go tinha **duas** falhas reais, e o diagnóstico inicial do log escondia a causa principal.

## Go debug — causa raiz

Reproduzi contra o `dlv` instalado da própria IDE e a resposta real do adaptador era:

```
Failed to launch /tmp/gotest/main.go: Go version go1.22.2 is too old for this
version of Delve (minimum supported version 1.25, suppress this error with --check-go-version=false)
```

O Delve 1.27.2 (o build que a IDE baixa) recusa iniciar com Go anterior a 1.25. Nosso código, então, ignorava essa falha de `launch`, esperava 90 s pelo evento `initialized` e depois enviava `setBreakpoints`, que o delve respondia com `No debug session started` — exatamente o que apareceu no seu log. Correções:

- `registry.json` e `dap_registry.json`: Go agora roda com `--check-go-version=false` (respeitar o gate deixaria o debug de Go inutilizável nesta máquina) e sem `--accept-multiclient`, que o `dlv dap` não suporta (só gerava o warning do log).
- `DapSession.awaitInitializedEvent` recebe o future do `launch` e aborta na hora quando o adaptador rejeita o launch, mostrando a mensagem real (build error, versão, etc.) em vez de esperar 90 s e reportar erro secundário.
- Segunda falha descoberta: mesmo com o launch funcionando, **a saída do programa Go não aparecia** — o delve escreve o stdout do debuggee no próprio stdout dele, que a IDE não lia. O adaptador Go agora usa `outputMode: "remote"`, e a saída chega como eventos `output` do DAP, com os prefixos `[OUTPUT]`/`[ERROR]` normais.

## Saída copiável e Stop no Run

- O painel OUTPUT (`IOPanel`) era `setFocusable(false)`, o que impedia qualquer cópia pelo teclado. Agora é somente-leitura mas selecionável, com `Ctrl+C`/`Cmd+C` mapeados, menu de contexto com *Copy* e *Select All*, e tooltip explicando.
- Modo de execução sem debug agora mostra um botão **Stop** (só ele; os botões de depuração continuam exclusivos do debug). Ele para o processo via `AbstractLanguage.forceStop` numa worker thread do `ThreadMaster`, para não bloquear a EDT enquanto o processo morre, e o painel volta ao estado ocioso quando a linguagem reporta a interrupção.

## Testes

- `GoDebugAdapterIntegrationTest`: removido o skip `goVersionAtLeast(25)` que mascarava o problema; os dois testes (módulo e `.go` avulso sem `go.mod`) agora rodam de verdade, com breakpoint, resume e verificação de `doubled=2`. Também afirmam os argumentos do adaptador (`--check-go-version=false`, sem `--accept-multiclient`).
- `DapSessionIntegrationTest.reportsTheLaunchErrorInsteadOfWaitingForTheInitializedEvent` (novo): `FakeDapServer` ganhou `--fail-launch <msg>` e o teste garante que a mensagem real sai em < 25 s.
- `IOPanelTest`: +2 testes (Stop só no Run; saída selecionável com `Ctrl+C`).
- `IOPanelRunStopIntegrationTest` (novo, com `RunStopProbe`): sobe um processo real, clica no Stop e confirma que ele morre e o painel volta ao normal.

Verificações executadas: `make test-debug` → 22 testes, 0 falhas, **0 skips** (antes o Go era skipado); `make test` → 452 testes, 0 falhas, 11 skips; `make check-format` OK. Docs atualizadas em `docs/reference/DAP.md` e `docs/api/dap.md` (seção "Go and older toolchains", saída remota, fail-fast do launch, saída copiável e Stop do Run).

Limitação: não rodei a GUI (sem display aqui), então o clique real nos botões e o `Ctrl+C` no painel foram verificados por testes de unidade/integração, não visualmente. Nada foi commitado.

Corrigi o passo do Mono em `.github/workflows/debug.yml`, que é onde o seu comando aparecia.

**Causa do erro de keyring**

O `echo` do repositório aponta para `[signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg]`, mas *nada cria esse arquivo*. No workflow a chave era importada por `keyserver.ubuntu.com`; quando o keyserver não responde (comum nos runners), o `gpg --recv-keys` não escreve a keyring e o `apt-get update` falha com `NO_PUBKEY`/keyring ausente — exatamente o erro que você viu. Se você usou só a linha do `echo` na sua máquina, o efeito é o mesmo: `signed-by` apontando para um arquivo inexistente.

**O que mudou**

- Chave baixada por HTTPS direto de `https://download.mono-project.com/repo/xamarin.gpg` (o endereço oficial), com `--retry 3` — sem depender de keyserver.
- `gpg --dearmor` grava `/etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg` com `--batch --yes`.
- A fingerprint é conferida depois do download (`3FA7E0328081BFF6A14DA29AA6A19B38D3D831EF`); chave errada ou corrompida falha no passo, em vez de virar erro confuso do apt.
- `set -euo pipefail` e `curl` incluído nos pacotes instalados.

**Verificações feitas**

- Baixei a chave real: HTTP 200, 2125 bytes, conteúdo é bloco PGP público e a fingerprint primária é exatamente `3FA7E0328081BFF6A14DA29AA6A19B38D3D831EF` (mesma que o `--recv-keys` antigo pedia) — então a troca de origem não muda a chave.
- Rodei o trecho do passo (com `sudo`/apt removidos e paths em `/tmp`) com `set -euo pipefail`: exit 0 e keyring de 1496 bytes gerada, e a checagem de fingerprint passou.
- `yaml.safe_load` do workflow OK (10 steps) e `bash -n` no script do passo OK.

Não rodei o job no GitHub Actions (sem push autorizado), então o passo novo ainda não foi exercitado em runner real.

**Na sua máquina**, para o repositório do Mono funcionar, recrie a keyring antes do `apt-get update`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.mono-project.com/repo/xamarin.gpg \
  | sudo gpg --batch --yes --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg
sudo gpg --show-keys --with-colons /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg | grep 3FA7E032
