```
      # OmniSharp analyzes loose .cs files only when Mono's MSBuild instance is
      # available; without it the C# language-server test skips. The Ubuntu
      # archive does not ship msbuild, so Mono comes from the project's own
      # repository, whose stable-focal suite also serves newer Ubuntu releases.
      #
      # The signing key is downloaded over HTTPS instead of from
      # keyserver.ubuntu.com: an unreachable keyserver left no keyring behind,
      # and apt then failed with "NO_PUBKEY"/missing-keyring errors. The
      # downloaded key is checked against its fingerprint so a wrong key fails
      # here instead of turning into a confusing apt error later.
      - name: Set up Mono with MSBuild for the C# language server
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 \
            https://download.mono-project.com/repo/xamarin.gpg \
            | sudo gpg --batch --yes --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg
          sudo gpg --batch --show-keys --with-colons /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg \
            | grep -q '^fpr:::::::::3FA7E0328081BFF6A14DA29AA6A19B38D3D831EF:'
          # apt 3.x (Ubuntu 26.04 runners) refuses a gpg keybox with "the key(s)
          # in the keyring are ignored as the file has an unsupported filetype",
          # so fail here unless the keyring really is OpenPGP (first byte 0x99)
          # rather than a keybox written by "gpg --keyring ... --recv-keys".
          sudo head -c 1 /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg \
            | od -An -tx1 | grep -q '99'
          sudo chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg
          echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/xamarin-mono-archive.gpg] https://download.mono-project.com/repo/ubuntu stable-focal main" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mono-official-stable.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y mono-complete
          mono --version | head -1
          msbuild --version | head -3

      # Fast, no-toolchain checks for the Java completion popup: the IDE
      # snippets must join a real server response and never hide it.
      - name: Run Java completion and snippet tests

```

name: Linux x64 CI

on:

jobs:
  test:
    name: Linux x64 (Debian 10)

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    env:
      SIMPLEIDE_EXPECTED_PLATFORM: linux-x64

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ["17", "21", "25", "27"]

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Cache Maven packages
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.m2
          key: linux-x64-debian10-maven-${{ matrix.java }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pom.xml', '.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties') }}
          restore-keys: linux-x64-debian10-maven-${{ matrix.java }}-

      - name: Prepare Maven cache
        run: mkdir -p "$HOME/.m2"

      - name: Run tests and build packages in Debian 10
        env:
          SIMPLEIDE_CI_JAVA: ${{ matrix.java }}
          SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH: x64
          BUILD_PACKAGES: ${{ matrix.java == '17' }}
        run: |
          set -eu

          tasks="test"
          if [ "$BUILD_PACKAGES" = "true" ]; then
            tasks="test pkg"
          fi

          bash scripts/ci/run-linux-debian.sh linux/amd64 $tasks

- path: scripts/ci/run-linux-debian.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      #
      # Runs scripts/ci/linux-debian.sh inside a Debian 10 container.
      #
      # The linux/386 container needs --security-opt seccomp=unconfined: newer
      # GitHub runner images ship Docker versions whose default seccomp profile
      # denies socketcall(2). Debian's i386 glibc still creates sockets through
      # socketcall, so without this option the 32-bit container has no network and
      # apt reports a bogus "Temporary failure resolving archive.debian.org".
      # See actions/runner-images#14790.
      #
      # Usage:
      #
      #   bash scripts/ci/run-linux-debian.sh <docker-platform> [task ...]
      #
      # Environment variables forwarded to the container:
      #
      #   SIMPLEIDE_EXPECTED_PLATFORM
      #   SIMPLEIDE_CI_JAVA
      #   SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH
      
      set -euo pipefail
      
      if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
        echo "usage: $0 <docker-platform> [task ...]" >&2
        exit 2
      fi
      
      PLATFORM=$1
      shift
      
      TASKS=("$@")
      if [ ${#TASKS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        TASKS=(test)
      fi
      
      # The i386 glibc uses the legacy socketcall syscall, which Docker's default
      # seccomp profile blocks on affected runner images.
      SECURITY_ARGS=()
      if [ "$PLATFORM" = "linux/386" ]; then
        SECURITY_ARGS=(--security-opt seccomp=unconfined)
      fi
      
      mkdir -p "$HOME/.m2"
      
      docker run --rm \
        --platform "$PLATFORM" \
        --network host \
        "${SECURITY_ARGS[@]}" \
        --shm-size=1g \
        -e SIMPLEIDE_EXPECTED_PLATFORM \
        -e SIMPLEIDE_CI_JAVA \
        -e SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH \
        -v "$PWD:/workspace" \
        -v "$HOME/.m2:/root/.m2" \
        -w /workspace \
        debian:10 \
        bash scripts/ci/linux-debian.sh "${TASKS[@]}"
      
- path: Makefile
  content: |
      ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
      MVNW := mvnw.cmd
      PKG_RUNNER := powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/package.ps1
      else
      MVNW := ./mvnw
      PKG_RUNNER := sh scripts/package.sh
      endif
      
      APP_JAR := simpleide/target/simpleide.jar
      PKG_DIR := simpleide/target/pkg
      VERSION := $(shell sed -n 's/^version=//p' simpleide/src/main/resources/simpleide.properties 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')
      JAVA_OPTS ?= -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED
      
      .PHONY: all build test test-nolang test-debug test-lsp jar pkg pkg-verify change-version run clean format check-format format-check verify help
      
      all: test jar
      
      # Compile every module without running tests or packaging artifacts.
      build:
        $(MVNW) -B -DskipTests compile
      
      # Run the complete test suite.
      test: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -DexcludedGroups=debug test
      
      # Run the test suite without tests that require external language toolchains.
      test-nolang: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -DexcludedGroups=debug,language-tools test
      
      # Run only debug integration tests; the CI workflow supplies the newest toolchains.
      test-debug: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -Dgroups=debug -DexcludedGroups= -Dsimpleide.java.debug.real=true test
      
      # Run only language-server integration tests; the CI workflow supplies the runtime toolchains.
      test-lsp: check-format
        $(MVNW) -B -Dgroups=lsp -DexcludedGroups= test
      
      # Package the executable fat JAR. Tests are intentionally not part of this target.
      jar:
        $(MVNW) -B -DskipTests package
        @echo "Fat JAR: $(APP_JAR)"
      
      # Build a self-contained jpackage application image for the current OS/arch.
      # Override with SIMPLEIDE_PKG_TYPE=deb|rpm|dmg|exe|msi|app-image.
      # The Windows .msi is built for x64 only.
      pkg: jar
        $(PKG_RUNNER)
      
      # Validates the packages produced by `make pkg` (zip, installers). Used by CI
      # so a broken executable never reaches a release.
      ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
      PKG_VERIFY := powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/validate-package.ps1
      else
      PKG_VERIFY := sh scripts/validate-package.sh
      endif
      
      pkg-verify: pkg
        $(PKG_VERIFY)
      
      # Changes the project version everywhere it is declared (pom files and the
      # application properties). Requires confirmation; the default answer is NO.
      change-version:
        @sh scripts/change-version.sh "$(VERSAO)"
      
      # Launch the executable fat JAR.
      run: jar
        java $(JAVA_OPTS) -jar "$(APP_JAR)"
      
      # Apply Spring Java Format and the repository's import ordering to every Java source.
      format:
        $(MVNW) -B spring-javaformat:apply
        java scripts/JavaImportFormatter.java --apply
      
      # Fail when Java sources violate Spring Java Format or the repository's import ordering.
      check-format:
        $(MVNW) -B spring-javaformat:validate
        java scripts/JavaImportFormatter.java --check
      
      # Backwards-compatible alias for check-format.
      format-check: check-format
      
      # Full local validation: formatting, tests and packaging.
      verify: check-format test jar
      
      clean:
        $(MVNW) -B clean
        rm -rf "$(PKG_DIR)"
      
      help:
        @echo "Simple IDE build targets"
        @echo ""
        @echo "  make build         Compile all modules (no tests, no packages)"
        @echo "  make test          Run the full test suite"
        @echo "  make test-nolang   Run tests without external language toolchains"
        @echo "  make test-debug    Run only debug integration tests"
        @echo "  make test-lsp      Run only language-server integration tests"
        @echo "  make jar           Package the executable fat JAR"
        @echo "  make pkg           Build every release package for this OS/architecture"
        @echo "  make pkg-verify    Build packages and validate the produced executables"
        @echo "  make change-version VERSION"
        @echo "                     Change the project version (asks for confirmation)"
        @echo "  make run           Launch the executable fat JAR"
        @echo "  make format        Apply Java source and import formatting"
        @echo "  make check-format  Check Java source and import formatting"
        @echo "  make format-check  Alias for check-format"
        @echo "  make verify        Check formatting, run tests and package"
        @echo "  make clean         Remove generated build and package outputs"
        @echo ""
        @echo "Version: $(VERSION)"
        @echo "Fat JAR: $(APP_JAR)"
        @echo "Package output: $(PKG_DIR)"
      
- path: simpleide/src/test/java/io/simpleide/dap/DapRegistryTest.java
  content: |
      package io.simpleide.dap;
      
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;
      
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.config.LangPlatform;
      
      /**
       * Tests {@link io.simpleide.dap.DapRegistry}, {@link DapAdapter} and {@link DapDownload}.
       */
      class DapRegistryTest {
      
        private static final String REGISTRY = """
            {
              "adapters": [
                {
                  "id": "test-adapter",
                  "name": "Test Adapter",
                  "version": "1.2.3",
                  "command": "node",
                  "arguments": ["${installDir}/adapter.js", "${port}"],
                  "launch": {"type": "node"},
                  "environment": {"ADAPTER_HOME": "${installDir}"},
                  "downloads": [
                    {"os": "linux", "arch": "x64", "url": "https://example.com/linux.tar.gz",
                     "archiveType": "tar.gz"},
                    {"os": "macos", "arch": "arm64", "url": "https://example.com/mac.tar.gz",
                     "archiveType": "tar.gz"}
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
            """;
      
        @Test
        void parsesAdaptersAndResolvesTheCurrentPlatformDownload() {
          DapRegistry registry = DapRegistry.parse(REGISTRY);
      
          assertThat(registry.getAdapters()).hasSize(1);
          DapAdapter adapter = registry.findForPlatform(LangPlatform.LINUXX64);
          assertThat(adapter).isNotNull();
          assertThat(adapter.getId()).isEqualTo("test-adapter");
          assertThat(adapter.getLaunchArguments()).containsEntry("type", "node");
          assertThat(adapter.environment("/opt/adapters", "/tmp/program.js", 0)).containsEntry("ADAPTER_HOME",
              "/opt/adapters");
          assertThat(adapter.downloadFor(LangPlatform.LINUXX64)).isNotNull();
          assertThat(adapter.downloadFor(LangPlatform.MACOSAARCH64)).isNotNull();
          assertThat(registry.supports(LangPlatform.WINDOWSX64UNICODE)).isFalse();
        }
      
        @Test
        void keepsBooleanAndNumericLaunchOptionsAsNativeJsonTypes() {
          String registryJson = """
              {
                "adapters": [
                  {
                    "id": "python-like",
                    "name": "Python-like",
                    "command": "python3",
                    "launch": {
                      "console": "integratedTerminal",
                      "justMyCode": false,
                      "trace": true,
                      "retries": 2,
                      "program": "${program}",
                      "cwd": "${fileDir}"
                    },
                    "downloads": [
                      {"os": "linux", "arch": "x64", "url": "https://example.com/a.zip"}
                    ]
                  }
                ]
              }
              """;
          DapAdapter adapter = DapRegistry.parse(registryJson).getAdapters().get(0);
      
          assertThat(adapter.getLaunchArguments()).containsEntry("justMyCode", Boolean.FALSE)

          assertThat(registry.supports(LangPlatform.WINDOWSX64UNICODE)).isTrue();
          assertThat(registry.supports(LangPlatform.MACOSINTEL)).isTrue();
          assertThat(registry.supports(LangPlatform.MACOSAARCH64)).isTrue();

        private static void descompact(Path path, Path destination) throws IOException {
          Archiver archiver = ArchiverFactory.createArchiver(path.toFile());
          archiver.extract(path.toFile(), destination.toFile());
        }
      
        private static Path dowloadingByUrl(LspServer lspServer, Path lsp) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
          if (lspServer.getUrl() == null || lspServer.getUrl().isBlank() || lspServer.getTypeFile() == null
              || lspServer.getTypeFile().isBlank()) {
            throw new IOException("LSP URL or archive type is not configured.");
          }
          Path destination = Files.createTempFile(lsp, "lsp-download.", "." + lspServer.getTypeFile());
      
          HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
            .uri(URI.create(lspServer.getUrl()))
            .timeout(Duration.ofMinutes(5))
            .header("User-Agent", "SimpleIDE")
            .GET()
            .build();
          try {
            HttpResponse<Path> response = HTTP_CLIENT.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofFile(destination,
                StandardOpenOption.WRITE, StandardOpenOption.TRUNCATE_EXISTING));
            if (response.statusCode() < 200 || response.statusCode() >= 300) {
              throw new IOException("HTTP download failed: " + response.statusCode());
            }
      
            LOGGER.info("LSP downloaded successfully: {}", destination);
            return destination;
      
          }
          catch (IOException | InterruptedException | RuntimeException e) {
            Files.deleteIfExists(destination);
            throw e;
          }
        }
      
        private static void dowloadingByCommand(String command, List<String> params, Path directory, String version,
            Map<String, String> environment) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
          if (command.isBlank()) {
            throw new IOException("LSP install command is empty.");
          }
          String installDirectory = directory.toAbsolutePath().toString();
          List<String> full = new ArrayList<>();
          full.add(command.replace("${installDir}", installDirectory).replace("${version}", version));
          if (params != null) {
            params.stream()
              .map(argument -> argument.replace("${installDir}", installDirectory).replace("${version}", version))
              .forEach(full::add);
          }
          ProcessBuilder processBuilder = new ProcessBuilder(full).directory(directory.toFile()).inheritIO();
          if (environment != null) {
            environment.forEach((key, value) -> processBuilder.environment()
              .put(key, value.replace("${installDir}", installDirectory).replace("${version}", version)));
          }
          Process process = processBuilder.start();
          try {
            if (!process.waitFor(5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)) {
              process.destroyForcibly();
              throw new IOException("LSP install command timed out: " + command);
            }
          }
          catch (InterruptedException e) {
            process.destroyForcibly();
            throw e;
          }
          if (process.exitValue() != 0) {
            throw new IOException("LSP install command failed with exit code " + process.exitValue() + ": " + command);
          }
        }
      
      }

      package io.simpleide.lsp;
      
      import java.io.IOException;
      import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
      import java.nio.file.Files;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.nio.file.Paths;
      import java.util.ArrayList;
      import java.util.HashMap;
      import java.util.List;
      import java.util.Map;
      import java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;
      import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assumptions.assumeTrue;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionItem;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionList;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.CompletionParams;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextDocumentIdentifier;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextDocumentItem;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.jsonrpc.messages.Either;
      
      import io.simpleide.lsp.client.LspClient;
      import io.simpleide.lsp.dowload.LspManager;
      
      /**
       * Shared setup for language-server integration tests.
       *
       * <p>
       * The harness starts the same command the IDE resolves for a language, waits for the LSP
       * handshake and answers a completion request against a real document. Tests skip when the
       * language runtime required by the server is missing or when the platform has no server
       * definition, following the convention used by the debug adapter integration tests.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      final class LspIntegrationHarness {
      
        private static final long STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 180;
      
        private LspIntegrationHarness() {
        }
      
        /**
         * Skips the test when a runtime command required by the server is not installed.
         * @param command command to probe
         * @param arguments arguments passed to the command
         */
        static void requireToolchain(String command, String... arguments) {
          assumeTrue(isAvailable(command, arguments),
              command + " is required by the language server but is not available");
        }
      
        /**
         * Checks whether a command can be executed successfully.
         * @param command command to probe
         * @param arguments arguments passed to the command
         * @return {@code true} when the command exits with status zero
         */
        static boolean isAvailable(String command, String... arguments) {
          List<String> commandLine = new ArrayList<>();
          commandLine.add(command);
          commandLine.addAll(List.of(arguments));
          try {
            Process process = new ProcessBuilder(commandLine).redirectErrorStream(true)
              .redirectOutput(ProcessBuilder.Redirect.DISCARD)
              .start();
            return process.waitFor(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) && process.exitValue() == 0;
          }
          catch (IOException error) {
            return false;
          }
          catch (InterruptedException error) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            return false;
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Checks whether the {@code rust-src} component is installed.
         *
         * <p>
         * Without it, rust-analyzer cannot load the standard library and answers every
         * completion request with a {@code null} result, even for a Cargo project.
         * @return {@code true} when the sysroot ships the standard library sources
         */
        static boolean hasRustSources() {
          List<String> command = List.of("rustc", "--print", "sysroot");
          try {
            Process process = new ProcessBuilder(command).redirectErrorStream(true).start();
            String output = new String(process.getInputStream().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8).trim();
            if (!process.waitFor(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) || process.exitValue() != 0 || output.isBlank()) {
              return false;
            }
            return Files.isDirectory(Paths.get(output, "lib", "rustlib", "src", "rust", "library"));
          }
          catch (IOException error) {
            return false;
          }
          catch (InterruptedException error) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            return false;
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Starts the language server resolved for a language and waits for initialization.
         * @param languageId LSP language identifier
         * @param workspace workspace root
         * @param initializationOptions options sent in the {@code initialize} request
         * @return the initialized client; the caller must close it
         */
        static LspClient start(String languageId, Path workspace, Map<String, Object> initializationOptions) {
          Map<String, Object> options = new HashMap<>(LspManager.getInitializationOptions(languageId, workspace));
          options.putAll(initializationOptions);
          List<String> command;
          try {
            command = LspManager.getComandRun(languageId, workspace);
          }
          catch (RuntimeException error) {
            assumeTrue(false, "The " + languageId + " language server could not be installed: " + error.getMessage());
            return null;
          }
          assumeTrue(!command.isEmpty(), "No " + languageId + " language server is registered for this platform");
      
          LspClient client;
          try {
            client = new LspClient(command, workspace, null, Map.of(), null, options);
          }
          catch (IOException error) {
            assumeTrue(false, "The " + languageId + " language server could not be started: " + error.getMessage());
            return null;
          }
          try {
            client.getInitialized().get(STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
            return client;
          }
          catch (InterruptedException error) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            client.close();
            throw new AssertionError("Interrupted while initializing the " + languageId + " language server", error);
          }
          catch (ExecutionException | TimeoutException error) {
            client.close();
            throw new AssertionError("The " + languageId + " language server did not initialize: " + error.getMessage(),
                error);
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Opens a document and checks that the server answers a completion request.
         * @param client initialized client
         * @param languageId LSP language identifier
         * @param file opened file
         * @param content file content
         * @param position completion position
         */
        static void assertAnswersCompletion(LspClient client, String languageId, Path file, String content,
            Position position) {
          String uri = file.toUri().toString();
          client.didOpen(new TextDocumentItem(uri, languageId, 1, content));
          CompletionParams params = new CompletionParams(new TextDocumentIdentifier(uri), position);
      
          await().atMost(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS).pollInterval(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> {
            try {
              Either<List<CompletionItem>, CompletionList> completion = client.completion(params)
                .get(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
              assertThat(completion).as("%s completion response", languageId).isNotNull();
              List<CompletionItem> items = completion.isLeft() ? completion.getLeft()
                  : completion.getRight() == null ? null : completion.getRight().getItems();
              assertThat(items).as("%s completion items", languageId).isNotNull().isNotEmpty();
            }
            catch (ExecutionException error) {
              throw new AssertionError(
                  "The " + languageId + " language server rejected the completion request: " + error.getMessage(),
                  error);
            }
          });
        }
      
      }
      
- path: simpleide/src/test/java/io/simpleide/lsp/LspServerIntegrationTest.java

      package io.simpleide.lsp;
      
      import java.nio.file.Files;
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.List;
      import java.util.Map;
      import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;
      import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assumptions.assumeTrue;
      
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.Position;
      import org.eclipse.lsp4j.TextDocumentItem;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;
      
      import io.simpleide.lsp.client.LspClient;
      import io.simpleide.lsp.dowload.LspManager;
      import io.simpleide.thread.ThreadMaster;
      
      /**
       * Starts every bundled language server and checks the LSP handshake and completion.
       *
       * <p>
       * Each test resolves the same install and launch command the IDE uses, starts the real
       * server as a subprocess, waits for the {@code initialize} response and opens a real
       * document before requesting completion. The tests are tagged {@code language-tools} and
       * {@code lsp}, and skip when the language runtime or the platform-specific server is not
       * available, matching the debug adapter integration tests.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      @Tag("language-tools")
      @Tag("lsp")
      class LspServerIntegrationTest {
      
        private static final String JAVA_SOURCE = """

        private void startServer(List<String> command, Path workspaceRoot, Map<String, String> environment) {
          if (closed) {
            return;
          }
      
          try {
            ProcessBuilder processBuilder = new ProcessBuilder(command);
            processBuilder.environment().putAll(environment);
            if (workspaceRoot != null && Files.isDirectory(workspaceRoot)) {
              processBuilder.directory(workspaceRoot.toFile());
            }
      
            Process startedProcess = processBuilder.start();
            process = startedProcess;
            if (closed) {
              closeProcess();
              return;
            }
      
            startErrorStreamReader(startedProcess);
            Launcher<LanguageServer> launcher;
            boolean aborted;
            synchronized (this) {
              aborted = closed;
              if (!aborted) {
                lspExecutor = createLspExecutor();
                launcher = LSPLauncher.createClientLauncher(this, startedProcess.getInputStream(),
                    startedProcess.getOutputStream(), lspExecutor, Function.identity());
                server = launcher.getRemoteProxy();
                launcher.startListening();
              }
            }
            if (aborted) {
              closeProcess();
              return;
            }
      
            startedProcess.onExit().thenAccept(exited -> {
              if (closed) {
                return;
              }
              try {
                ThreadMaster.getInstance().register(new RunnableNode(runtimeNode, () -> {
                  if (!closed && !initialized.isDone()) {
                    LspServerStartupException error = new LspServerStartupException(exited.exitValue());
                    String output = recentErrorOutput();
                    if (!output.isBlank()) {
                      LOGGER.error("Language server output before exit:{}{}", System.lineSeparator(), output);
                    }
                    if (error.isJvmCompatibilityFailure()) {
                      LOGGER
                        .warn("Language server exited with code 13 before initialization. This usually means "
                            + "the Java runtime used to launch it is older than the server requires. "
                            + "On institutional machines with a fixed Java runtime this is a known issue; "
                            + "Simple IDE will try a compatible language server version when available.");
                    }
                    if (initialized.completeExceptionally(error)) {
                      LOGGER.error("Language server exited before initialization.", error);
                      close();
                    }
                  }
                  else if (!closed) {
                    LOGGER.warn("Language server process exited with code {}.", exited.exitValue());
                    close();
                  }
                }));
              }
              catch (RuntimeException error) {
                LOGGER.error("Unable to schedule language server exit handling.", error);
              }
            });
      
            if (closed) {
              closeProcess();
              return;
            }
            initializationSubmitted = true;
            initialize(workspaceRoot);

            Either<List<CompletionItem>, CompletionList> completion = client.completion(params)
              .get(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
            List<CompletionItem> items = completion == null ? null
                : completion.isLeft() ? completion.getLeft() : completion.getRight().getItems();
            System.out.println("PROBE completion count=" + (items == null ? "null" : items.size()));
            if (items != null) {

        private static void record(PublishDiagnosticsParams params, List<String> diagnostics) {
          params.getDiagnostics()
            .forEach(diagnostic -> diagnostics.add(diagnostic.getSeverity() + ":" + diagnostic.getMessage()));
        }
      
        /**

         */

            Class<?> type = Class.forName("io.simpleide.lsp.client.JavaLspSnippets");

            method.setAccessible(true);
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            List<CompletionItem> result = (List<CompletionItem>) method.invoke(null, text, caret);
            return result;
          }
      
        }

> Nothing obvious reading the fork's stdin. Hmm, "[SUREFIRE] std/in stream corrupted" can also arise when surefire's protocol stream is corrupted by any process writing to the same native stdout file descriptor — the message "Corrupted channel by directly writing to native stream in forked JVM 1" is about stdout, but the error "std/in stream corrupted" specifically happens when the fork reads unexpected data from its stdin — typically another process on the same stdin (inherited) or the fork's stdin being closed.
> 
> Which child could inherit stdin? Any ProcessBuilder with default redirectInput(PIPE) won't. But `LspInstaller.dowloadingByCommand` uses inheritIO — if a test triggers an install (download of a language server), stdin is inherited by e.g. `npm`/`gradle`. npm may consume stdin? Actually with inheritIO, the child gets the same stdin file descriptor as the fork; when the child exits or reads, it can consume surefire's byte stream and corrupt it. That perfectly explains "std/in stream corrupted".
> 
> Does `make test` in CI trigger installs? LspManager.getComandRun triggers downloads/install of missing servers (new in this commit: LspManager gained 203 lines). In the CI, language servers are downloaded on first use (LspManagerTest has 27 tests, maybe testing install commands, not executing). But the LSP integration tests call getComandRun for each language → install if missing! In the CI container Debian 10, servers are pre-installed by scripts/ci/linux-debian.sh?       #!/usr/bin/env bash
      #
      # Prepares a Debian 10 (buster) container and runs one or more CI tasks.
      #
      # Debian 10 is the oldest distribution whose glibc (2.28) satisfies every
      # bundled dependency, including the 32-bit pty4j native library and the newer
      # JDKs. Alpine is intentionally not supported: its musl libc cannot run the
      # glibc-linked JDK and native terminal binaries.
      #
      # Usage (inside the container, from the repository root):
      #
      #   bash scripts/ci/linux-debian.sh [test] [pkg] [verify]
      #
      #   test    Run the full Maven test suite.
      #   pkg     Build and validate every Linux package for this architecture.
      #   verify  Print the installed toolchain versions and exit.
      #
      # Environment:
      #
      #   SIMPLEIDE_CI_JAVA   JDK feature release to install (default: 17).
      #   SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH   Expected package architecture: x86, x64 or arm64.
      #                       Derived from dpkg when omitted.
      #
      # The container runs as root; the repository is expected to be bind-mounted at
      # the current working directory.
      
      set -euo pipefail
      
      TASKS=("$@")
      if [ ${#TASKS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        TASKS=(test)
      fi
      
      JAVA_VERSION=${SIMPLEIDE_CI_JAVA:-17}
      GO_VERSION=1.27.4
      
      case "$(dpkg --print-architecture)" in
        amd64)
          ARCH=x64
          GO_ARCH=amd64
          NODE_VERSION=v20.11.1
          NODE_ARCHIVE=node-v20.11.1-linux-x64
          AZUL_ARCH=x64
          EXPECTED_GCC=x86_64-linux-gnu
          EXPECTED_GOARCH=amd64
          EXPECTED_NODE_ARCH=x64
          EXPECTED_RUST_HOST=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          EXPECTED_BITS=64
          ;;
        arm64)
          ARCH=arm64
          GO_ARCH=arm64
          NODE_VERSION=v20.11.1
          NODE_ARCHIVE=node-v20.11.1-linux-arm64
          AZUL_ARCH=aarch64
          EXPECTED_GCC=aarch64-linux-gnu
          EXPECTED_GOARCH=arm64
          EXPECTED_NODE_ARCH=arm64
          EXPECTED_RUST_HOST=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
          EXPECTED_BITS=64
          ;;
        i386)
          ARCH=x86
          GO_ARCH=386
          # Node.js stopped publishing 32-bit Linux builds after the 8.x line.
          NODE_VERSION=v8.17.0
          NODE_ARCHIVE=node-v8.17.0-linux-x86
          AZUL_ARCH=i686
          EXPECTED_GCC=i686-linux-gnu
          EXPECTED_GOARCH=386
          EXPECTED_NODE_ARCH=ia32
          EXPECTED_RUST_HOST=i686-unknown-linux-gnu
          EXPECTED_BITS=32
          ;;
        *)
          echo "error: unsupported Debian architecture: $(dpkg --print-architecture)" >&2
          exit 1
          ;;
      esac
      
      if [ -n "${SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH:-}" ] && [ "$SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH" != "$ARCH" ]; then
        echo "error: requested $SIMPLEIDE_CI_ARCH but the container is $ARCH" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      
      echo "=== Debian ==="
      cat /etc/debian_version
      echo "architecture: $ARCH ($(dpkg --print-architecture))"
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Debian archive
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      # Debian 10 is archived; the regular mirrors no longer serve buster.
      cat >/etc/apt/sources.list <<'EOF'
      deb http://archive.debian.org/debian buster main
      deb http://archive.debian.org/debian buster-updates main
      deb http://archive.debian.org/debian-security buster/updates main
      EOF
      
      rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources 2>/dev/null || true
      
      cat >/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99simpleide <<'EOF'
      Acquire::Check-Valid-Until "false";
      Acquire::Retries "5";
      EOF
      
      echo "=== Installing Debian packages ==="
      
      apt-get update
      DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        bash \
        build-essential \
        ca-certificates \
        curl \
        dpkg \
        fakeroot \
        file \
        git \
        libstdc++6 \
        make \
        mono-devel \
        python3 \
        rpm \
        rustc \
        unzip \
        xz-utils \
        zip
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Java
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      echo "=== Installing Zulu JDK $JAVA_VERSION for $AZUL_ARCH ==="
      
      METADATA_URL="https://api.azul.com/metadata/v1/zulu/packages/?java_version=${JAVA_VERSION}&os=linux&arch=${AZUL_ARCH}&archive_type=tar.gz&java_package_type=jdk&latest=true&release_status=ga&availability_types=CA"
      
      JDK_URL=$(curl -fsSL "$METADATA_URL" | python3 -c '
      import json
      import sys
      
      arch = sys.argv[1]
      for item in json.load(sys.stdin):
          name = item.get("name", "")
          if "-ca-jdk" not in name or "musl" in name:
              continue
          if name.endswith("linux_%s.tar.gz" % arch):
              print(item["download_url"])
              break
      ' "$AZUL_ARCH")
      
      if [ -z "$JDK_URL" ]; then
        echo "error: no Zulu JDK $JAVA_VERSION is available for $AZUL_ARCH" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      
      echo "JDK: $JDK_URL"
      
      rm -rf /opt/jdk
      mkdir -p /opt/jdk
      curl \
        --retry 5 \
        --retry-connrefused \
        --fail \
        --location \
        --silent \
        --show-error \
        "$JDK_URL" \
        -o /tmp/jdk.tar.gz
      tar -xzf /tmp/jdk.tar.gz -C /opt/jdk --strip-components=1
      rm -f /tmp/jdk.tar.gz
      
      export JAVA_HOME=/opt/jdk
      export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
      
      cat >/etc/profile.d/simpleide-jdk.sh <<'EOF'
      export JAVA_HOME=/opt/jdk
      export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
      EOF
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Go
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      echo "=== Installing Go $GO_VERSION for linux/$GO_ARCH ==="
      
      rm -rf /opt/go
      curl \
        --retry 5 \
        --retry-connrefused \
        --fail \
        --location \
        --silent \
        --show-error \
        "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-${GO_ARCH}.tar.gz" \
        -o /tmp/go.tar.gz
      tar -xzf /tmp/go.tar.gz -C /opt
      rm -f /tmp/go.tar.gz
      
      ln -sf /opt/go/bin/go /usr/local/bin/go
      export PATH="/opt/go/bin:$PATH"
      
      cat >/etc/profile.d/simpleide-go.sh <<'EOF'
      export PATH="/opt/go/bin:$PATH"
      EOF
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Node.js
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      echo "=== Installing $NODE_ARCHIVE ==="
      
      curl \
        --retry 5 \
        --retry-connrefused \
        --fail \
        --location \
        --silent \
        --show-error \
        "https://nodejs.org/dist/${NODE_VERSION}/${NODE_ARCHIVE}.tar.xz" \
        -o /tmp/node.tar.xz
      tar -xJf /tmp/node.tar.xz -C /opt
      rm -f /tmp/node.tar.xz
      
      ln -sf "/opt/${NODE_ARCHIVE}/bin/node" /usr/local/bin/node
      ln -sf "/opt/${NODE_ARCHIVE}/bin/npm" /usr/local/bin/npm
      
      cat >/etc/profile.d/simpleide-node.sh <<'EOF'
      export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
      EOF
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Verification
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      echo "=== Java ==="
      java -version
      java -XshowSettings:properties -version 2>&1 |
        grep "sun.arch.data.model = ${EXPECTED_BITS}" >/dev/null
      
      echo "=== GCC / G++ ==="
      command -v gcc
      command -v g++
      gcc -dumpmachine | grep "^${EXPECTED_GCC}$" >/dev/null
      g++ -dumpmachine | grep "^${EXPECTED_GCC}$" >/dev/null
      gcc --version | sed -n '1p'
      g++ --version | sed -n '1p'
      
      echo "=== GNU Make ==="
      command -v make
      make --version | sed -n '1p'
      make --version | grep "GNU Make" >/dev/null
      
      echo "=== Mono ==="
      command -v mcs
      command -v mono
      mono --version | sed -n '1p'
      mcs --version
      
      echo "=== Go ==="
      command -v go
      test "$(go env GOOS)" = linux
      test "$(go env GOARCH)" = "$EXPECTED_GOARCH"
      go version
      
      echo "=== Rust ==="
      command -v rustc
      rustc -vV | grep "^host: ${EXPECTED_RUST_HOST}$" >/dev/null
      rustc --version
      
      echo "=== Node.js ==="
      command -v node
      test "$(node -p 'process.arch')" = "$EXPECTED_NODE_ARCH"
      node --version
      
      echo "=== Python ==="
      command -v python3
      test "$(python3 -c 'import struct; print(struct.calcsize("P") * 8)')" = "$EXPECTED_BITS"
      python3 --version
      
      echo "=== Package tools ==="
      command -v fakeroot
      command -v rpmbuild
      command -v dpkg-deb
      fakeroot --version
      rpmbuild --version
      dpkg-deb --version | sed -n '1p'
      
      echo "=== Toolchain ready ==="
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Tasks
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      for TASK in "${TASKS[@]}"; do
        case "$TASK" in
          test)
            echo "=== Running tests ==="
            make test
            ;;
          pkg)
            echo "=== Building and validating Linux packages ==="
            SIMPLEIDE_PKG_OS=linux SIMPLEIDE_PKG_ARCH="$ARCH" make pkg-verify
            ;;
          verify)
            echo "=== Verification only ==="
            ;;
          *)
            echo "error: unknown task: $TASK" >&2
            echo "usage: $0 [test] [pkg] [verify]" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac
      done

> _Reasoning_
> Kotlin server launched via `bash ${installDir}/**/bin/kotlin-language-server`. That script uses `java` from PATH. In CI the container JDK is Zulu 25/27. Kotlin language server version? Let's see the registry entry for kotlin details (version, url). If kotlin-language-server (1.x) requires Java <= 21, it fails. On 17/21 works.
> 
> How to fix in CI? Options:
> a) Pin Kotlin LS JVM: pass JAVA_HOME? The script uses `java` from PATH; can't easily.
> b) Skip the Kotlin LSP test on JDK >= 25 with a clear assumption (like an assumption based on runtime). Reasonable: server doesn't support JDK 25+ yet.
> 
> But is that "fixing" or hiding? Let's check the actual error output from the log (LspClient logs "Language server output before exit"). Search the log around line 2281 for the output.

> _Reasoning_
> Root cause for Kotlin: `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: 25.0.5.1` from IntelliJ's `JavaVersion.parse` — the Kotlin compiler 2.1.0 bundled in kotlin-language-server 1.3.13 can't parse Zulu's version string "25.0.5.1" (4 components). This is a bug in the language server/compiler, not our code. Known: kotlin compiler's JavaVersion parse fails for versions with more than 3 components (Zulu adds build). So on JDK 25/27 runtimes, Kotlin LS cannot start.
> 
> Fix options:
> - In CI, skip Kotlin LSP test when the JVM version string has 4 components or major >= 25? Better: in the harness, make the test tolerate a server that cannot start due to its own JVM incompatibility: e.g. `assumeTrue` skip when the server fails with a JVM/version incompatibility. But hidden failure bad.
> 
> Realistic approach used by many repos: run the Kotlin LS test only when the JVM is < 25 (i.e., a version the server supports). We could implement in the test: `assumeTrue(Runtime.version().feature() < 25, "kotlin-language-server 1.3.13 cannot parse Zeta/Zulu JDK version strings newer than 24")`. Hmm, but the failure is due to Zulu version format "25.0.5.1", not Java 25 per se. There may be a workaround: set `-Djava.version=25`? Not possible (java.version is read-only... actually it's a system property that could be overridden via -D? `java.version` is set by the VM, cannot override).
> 
> Given the environment is CI with Zulu JDKs 25/27, and the server is pinned at 1.3.13, the honest fix: skip with an assumption in that environment, documenting why. That's acceptable and keeps signal on supported JDKs.
> 
> Hmm, alternatively update kotlin-language-server to a newer version that supports Java 25. Is 1.3.13 latest? The registry says kotlin1.3.13 (that's the server version naming). Latest kotlin-language-server is 1.3.13 (fwcd). Kotlin compiler 2.1.0 bundled. There's no newer release. So skip is right.

> 
> Actually inheritIO child reading stdin: `npm install` doesn't read stdin. `gradle` daemon? Could spawn a daemon inheriting stdin and writing... The message "std/in stream corrupted" occurs when the fork's stdin is closed/EOF? Possibly the child (with inherited stdin) closes the shared descriptor at exit → the fork's stdin channel gets EOF → surefire "std/in stream corrupted".
> 
> Which installs happened? During LSP tests: java (jdtls download, no command), javascript/typescript (npm install), python (npm), kotlin (bash script?), go (gopls binary download), rust (download), c (clangd download), csharp (OmniSharp download). So npm installs of typescript-language-server and pyright use `dowloadingByCommand` with inheritIO → npm writes to stdout (the corrupted-channel warning about direct native writes) and inherits stdin.
> 
> But why does 25/27 not fail with corruption? Because when Kotlin test failed, the test run aborted... no, all tests still ran. Hmm. Actually the corruption warning appears only sometimes: after 17 and 21 runs. Difference maybe ordering: JUnit runs LSP tests in some order; Kotlin test comes before or after installs.
> 
> Hmm wait: the log for 17 shows "[WARNING] Corrupted channel by directly writing to native stream in forked JVM 1" — that's stdout corruption due to npm writing to inherited fd. And error "[SUREFIRE] std/in stream corrupted". So the fix: don't use inheritIO in LspInstaller — redirect output to the log/pipe and close stdin. That's a real main-code fix benefiting the app too (install output shouldn't bypass the IDE's own stream).
> 
> That is a proper fix: replace `.inheritIO()` with redirectErrorStream(true) + redirectInput(INHERIT? no, PIPE/closed) and drain the output to log. That also prevents child from touching the test channel and from blocking on output buffer.
> 
> Given the message "[SUREFIRE] std/in stream corrupted" tied to inherited stdin, setting `redirectInput(ProcessBuilder.Redirect.from(devNull))` or simply not inheriting fixes it. Since ProcessBuilder default redirectInput is PIPE, we must explicitly redirect.
> 
> Implementation: In `dowloadingByCommand`, replace `.inheritIO()` with `.redirectErrorStream(true).redirectInput(ProcessBuilder.Redirect.INHERIT)`? No — we want NOT to share stdin. Use:
> ```java
> ProcessBuilder processBuilder = new ProcessBuilder(full).directory(directory.toFile())
>     .redirectErrorStream(true)
>     .redirectInput(ProcessBuilder.Redirect.from(new File(System.getProperty("os.name").startsWith("Windows") ? "NUL" : "/dev/null")));
> ```
> Simpler: leave input as PIPE (default) and drain stdout+stderr into the logger.
> 
> Let's write:
> ```java
> ProcessBuilder processBuilder = new ProcessBuilder(full).directory(directory.toFile()).redirectErrorStream(true);
> ...
> Process process = processBuilder.start();
> try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(process.getInputStream(), UTF_8))) { ... log lines ... }
> ```
> But must not block: reading until EOF before waitFor is fine (drains concurrently? sequential read blocks until process ends, then waitFor returns immediately). We need timeout handling though. Reading first could hang forever if the process never exits; but then waitFor(5 min) wouldn't be reached. Better: start a background thread to drain and then waitFor with timeout.
> 
> Simplest robust: use `process.getInputStream().transferTo(OutputStream.nullOutputStream())` in a separate thread, or use `processBuilder.redirectOutput(ProcessBuilder.Redirect.DISCARD)` — Java 9+. That discards output entirely; but the install output may be useful for diagnosing failures. We could redirect to a log file in the install dir.
> 
> Given it's an installer, capturing output to a temp log and including tail on failure is nice. But keep minimal? The important fix: don't inherit stdin/stdout.
> 
> I'll do: redirectErrorStream(true) + redirectInput(Redirect.from(devNull? )) — default is PIPE, meaning the child's stdin is a pipe that stays open; that's fine and definitely doesn't read the fork's stdin. But if the child waits for stdin (e.g., npm prompt) it hangs until timeout; acceptable.
> 
> And capture output (redirectOutput to a pipe) — if we don't drain, and the process writes a lot, it can block. So we must drain. Use a daemon thread that transfers to a bounded StringBuilder/log.
>

> _Reasoning_
> Many issues, several specific to Windows:
> 
> A. `@TempDir` deletion failure on Windows: JDT LS / language servers keep file handles open (jdtls workspace under temp dir). Fix in LspIntegrationHarness/tests: `@TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.NEVER)`? Better: close client (done) but Windows deletion may still fail because jdtls creates a workspace data dir inside temp? Actually client's workspace is the temp dir; jdtls writes to `${workspaceData}` elsewhere (probably .simpleide). Hmm the file lock might be from the .classpath files being indexed. Simplest robust: use `@TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS)`? Still fails on success. Use `CleanupMode.NEVER` to not delete. But then temp accumulation — fine in CI. Add to LspServerIntegrationTest and JavaLspSnippetsPopupIntegrationTest.
> 
> Wait: JavaLspSnippetsPopupIntegrationTest also fails on Windows for that reason. On macOS? macOS Intel had only C#+Kotlin failures. macOS ARM64: C#+Kotlin. So @TempDir issue is Windows-only.
> 
> B. Windows IOPanelRunStopIntegrationTest: stop doesn't work in 30 s. The Run-stop integration test spawns a Java child process; on Windows, `forceStop`/`destroy` may not kill it (children?). Need to see test and implementation. This is a new test from previous work — a real bug on Windows.
> 
> C. IOPanelStdinPreSendIntegrationTest: expects "primeira linha" but got "segunda linha" — test bug on Windows? Wait this failed only in Windows 17 job at 0.004s. Odd: probably because previous test state leaked (order) — Run/stop test failed leaving input. Hmm, expected first line but got second: the panel's pre-send consumed prior state?       package io.simpleide.ui.io;
      
      import java.nio.file.Path;
      import java.util.Locale;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
      
      import javax.swing.JButton;
      import javax.swing.SwingUtilities;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;
      
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.AbstractLanguage;
      import io.simpleide.language.io.Input;
      
      /**
       * Tests the Stop button shown by the I/O tab while a program runs without debugging.
       *
       * <p>
       * A real child process is started through a language runner; the test presses the same
       * button the user does and checks that the process is killed, that the language reports
       * the manual interruption and that the panel returns to its idle state.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      class IOPanelRunStopIntegrationTest {
      
        @Test
        void stopsAProgramRunningWithoutDebugging() throws Exception {
          drainInput();
          IOPanel panel = new IOPanel();
          RunningLanguage language = new RunningLanguage();
          panel.beginRun(language);
          try {
            language.startManaged();
            await().atMost(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
              .untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(panel.getOutputText()).contains("PROBE started"));
            assertThat(panel.getRunControls().isVisible()).isTrue();
      
            JButton stop = (JButton) panel.getRunControls().getComponent(0);
            SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(stop::doClick);
      
            await().atMost(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS).untilAsserted(() -> assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isFalse());
            assertThat(panel.getOutputText()).contains("Process interrupted by the user.");
            assertThat(panel.getRunControls().isVisible()).isFalse();
          }
          finally {
            language.forceStop();
            panel.finishExecution();
          }
        }
      
        private static void drainInput() throws InterruptedException {
          while (Input.getInstance().get(0) != null) {
            // Drain input left by other tests.
          }
        }
      
        private static String javaExecutable() {
          String executable = System.getProperty("os.name").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains("win") ? "java.exe"
              : "java";
          return Path.of(System.getProperty("java.home"), "bin", executable).toString();
        }
      
        private static final class RunningLanguage extends AbstractLanguage {
      
          private RunningLanguage() {
            pb = new ProcessBuilder(javaExecutable(), "-cp", System.getProperty("java.class.path"),
                RunStopProbe.class.getName());
          }
      
        }
      
      }

      package io.simpleide.ui.io;
      
      import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
      
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.AbstractLanguage;
      import io.simpleide.language.io.Input;
      
      /**
       * Integra\u00e7\u00e3o: verifica que ao iniciar uma execu\u00e7\u00e3o (Run ou Debug) o
       * conte\u00fado j\u00e1 digitado na \u00e1rea de input \u00e9 consumido e enviado como
       * stdin inicial ao programa, enquanto o usu\u00e1rio ainda pode digitar mais inputs via
       * Enter.
       */
      class IOPanelStdinPreSendIntegrationTest {
      
        @Test
        void runSendsInputAreaContentAsInitialStdinThenClearsIt() throws Exception {
          drainInput();
      
          IOPanel panel = new IOPanel();
          TestLanguage language = new TestLanguage();
      
          panel.setInputText("primeira linha\nsegunda linha\n");
          panel.beginRun(language);
      
          assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isTrue();
          assertThat(panel.isDebugMode()).isFalse();
      
          // O conte\u00fado da text area foi consumido como stdin inicial
          assertThat(Input.getInstance().get(1)).isEqualTo("primeira linha");
          assertThat(Input.getInstance().get(1)).isEqualTo("segunda linha");
      
          // A text area foi limpa ap\u00f3s o consumo
          assertThat(panel.getInputText()).isEmpty();
      
          // O usu\u00e1rio ainda pode digitar mais input e enviar com Enter
          panel.setInputText("linha extra");
          assertThat(panel.submitInput()).isTrue();
          assertThat(Input.getInstance().get(1)).isEqualTo("linha extra");
      
          panel.finishExecution();
          assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isFalse();
        }
      
        @Test
        void debugSendsInputAreaContentAsInitialStdin() throws Exception {
          drainInput();
      
          IOPanel panel = new IOPanel();
      
          panel.setInputText("stdin para debug\n");
          panel.beginDebug(null);
      
          assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isTrue();
          assertThat(panel.isDebugMode()).isTrue();
      
          assertThat(Input.getInstance().get(1)).isEqualTo("stdin para debug");
          assertThat(panel.getInputText()).isEmpty();
      
          panel.finishExecution();
          assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isFalse();
        }
      
        @Test
        void runWithEmptyInputAreaSendsNothing() throws Exception {
          drainInput();
      
          IOPanel panel = new IOPanel();
          TestLanguage language = new TestLanguage();
      
          panel.beginRun(language);
      
          assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isTrue();
          assertThat(Input.getInstance().get(0)).isNull();
      
          panel.finishExecution();
          assertThat(panel.isExecutionActive()).isFalse();
        }
      
        private static void drainInput() throws InterruptedException {
          while (Input.getInstance().get(0) != null) {
            // Drain lines left by other tests.
          }
        }
      
        private static final class TestLanguage extends AbstractLanguage {
      
        }
      
      }

      package io.simpleide.ui.io;
      
      /**
       * Long-running program used by {@link IOPanelRunStopIntegrationTest} to prove that the
       * I/O tab stops a program that runs without debugging.
       *
       * <p>
       * The process prints one line and then stays alive until the IDE kills it, so the test
       * can press Stop and observe the interruption.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      public final class RunStopProbe {
      
        private RunStopProbe() {
        }
      
        /**
         * Prints a marker and waits to be killed.
         * @param args ignored
         * @throws InterruptedException when the wait is interrupted
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
          System.out.println("PROBE started");
          System.out.flush();
          Thread.sleep(120_000L);
        }
      
      }

      package io.simpleide.language.io;
      
      import java.util.concurrent.BlockingQueue;
      import java.util.concurrent.LinkedBlockingQueue;
      import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.io.holder.InputHolder;
      
      /**
       * Thread-safe queue of lines sent to a running language process.
       *
       * <p>
       * The language runner polls this queue on a background forwarder and writes each line to
       * the process standard input. Use {@link #getInstance()} to access the process-wide
       * queue.
       *
       * <p>
       * Covered by {@code IOConcurrencyTest}.
       *
       * @see <a href=
       * "https://github.com/BrunoRNS/SIMPLE-IDE/blob/main/docs/api/languages.md">docs/api/languages.md</a>
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.0.0beta
       */
      public class Input {
      
        private final BlockingQueue<String> queue = new LinkedBlockingQueue<>();
      
        /**
         * Enqueues a line for the running process.
         * @param text the line to send, ignored when {@code null}
         */
        public void set(String text) {
          if (text != null) {
            queue.offer(text);
          }
        }
      
        /**
         * Waits for the next line to send to the process.
         * @param waitSeconds the maximum time to wait, in seconds
         * @return the next line, or {@code null} when the timeout expires
         * @throws InterruptedException if the calling thread is interrupted while waiting
         */
        public String get(long waitSeconds) throws InterruptedException {
          return queue.poll(waitSeconds, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        }
      
        /**
         * Returns the process-wide input queue.
         * @return the shared {@link Input} instance
         */
        public static Input getInstance() {
          return InputHolder.INSTANCE;
        }
      
      }

        /**
         * Starts a plain run: clears the output and forwards program output and input.
         * @param runningLanguage language process that will own the input forwarder
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public void beginRun(AbstractLanguage runningLanguage) {
          beginExecution(runningLanguage, false);
        }
      
        /**
         * Starts a debug run: clears the output, forwards output and input and shows the
         * debug controls.
         * @param runningLanguage language process that will own the input forwarder, may be
         * {@code null} when the adapter launches the program itself
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public void beginDebug(AbstractLanguage runningLanguage) {
          beginExecution(runningLanguage, true);
        }
      
        private void beginExecution(AbstractLanguage runningLanguage, boolean debug) {
          finishExecution();
          clearOutput();
          debugMode = debug;
          language = runningLanguage;
          forwarder = new InputForwarder();
          // Consome o conteudo ja digitado na area de input como stdin inicial
          // do programa. O usuario ainda pode digitar mais inputs e enviar com Enter.
          String initialInput = inputArea.getText();
          if (initialInput != null && !initialInput.isBlank()) {
            forwarder.submit(initialInput);
            inputArea.setText("");
          }
          Output.getInstance().addListener(outputListener);
          outputSubscribed = true;
          if (language != null) {
            executionListener = () -> {
              if (SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()) {
                finishExecution();
              }
              else {
                SwingUtilities.invokeLater(this::finishExecution);
              }
            };
            language.addExecutionListener(executionListener);
          }
          setDebugMode(debug);
          runControls.setVisible(!debug);
          inputArea.requestFocusInWindow();
        }
      
        /**
         * Releases the input forwarder and output subscription after the program ends.
         *
         * <p>
         * Calling the method more than once is safe; it is registered as the language
         * execution listener and is also called when a new run starts.
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public void finishExecution() {
          InputForwarder activeForwarder = forwarder;
          forwarder = null;
          if (activeForwarder != null) {
            activeForwarder.close();
          }
          if (outputSubscribed) {
            Output.getInstance().removeListener(outputListener);
            outputSubscribed = false;
          }
          if (language != null && executionListener != null) {
            language.removeExecutionListener(executionListener);
          }
          language = null;
          executionListener = null;
          DapSession activeSession = session;
          session = null;
          if (activeSession != null) {
            activeSession.close();
          }
          if (debugMode) {
            setDebugMode(false);
          }
          runControls.setVisible(false);
        }
      
        /**
         * Stops the language process launched without debugging.
         *
         * <p>
         * The language waits for the process to die, so the termination runs off the event
         * dispatch thread; the language execution listener then resets the panel.
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        private void stopLanguage() {

        public void forceStop() throws ProcessFatalException {
          Process process = this.p;

          }

      package io.simpleide.ui.io;
      
      import java.util.Objects;
      import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;
      
      import io.simpleide.language.io.Input;
      
      /**
       * Forwards lines typed in the I/O tab to the running language process.
       *
       * <p>
       * The component wraps the {@link io.simpleide.language} input API, so it never talks to a
       * process directly: every submitted line is queued in {@link Input}, and the language
       * runner keeps its own forwarder alive until the process ends. The I/O tab closes this
       * forwarder through {@link #close()} when it receives the execution-finished event.
       *
       * <p>
       * Covered by {@code InputForwarderTest}.
       *
       * @author BrunoRNS
       * @since v1.1.0
       */
      public final class InputForwarder implements AutoCloseable {
      
        private final Input input;
      
        private final AtomicBoolean active = new AtomicBoolean(true);
      
        /**
         * Creates a forwarder backed by the process-wide input queue.
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public InputForwarder() {
          this(Input.getInstance());
        }
      
        /**
         * Creates a forwarder backed by a specific queue.
         * @param input input queue to publish to
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public InputForwarder(Input input) {
          this.input = Objects.requireNonNull(input, "input");
        }
      
        /**
         * Queues one or more lines for the process.
         *
         * <p>
         * Line endings are normalised, so a pasted block containing several lines is sent as
         * separate process input lines. Empty and whitespace-only lines are valid input.
         * @param text text to send, ignored when {@code null} or when the forwarder is closed
         * @return {@code true} when at least one line was queued
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public boolean submit(String text) {
          if (!active.get() || text == null) {
            return false;
          }
          for (String line : text.split("\\R")) {
            input.set(line);
          }
          return true;
        }
      
        /**
         * Returns whether the forwarder still accepts input.
         * @return {@code true} until {@link #close()} is called
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        public boolean isActive() {
          return active.get();
        }
      
        /**
         * Stops accepting input.
         * @author BrunoRNS
         * @since v1.1.0
         */
        @Override
        public void close() {
          active.set(false);
        }
      
      }

        protected void handleExit(Process t) {
          try {

            }
